name: plains 123 km N of Labeatis Mensa
size_m: ~55 (50x64), a dark core with fainter darkening out to ~150 m
hirise: ESP_026180_2080 (2012-02-26, before the spot formed; not impact-targeted)
evidence: Compact dark spot about 55 m across (50 x 64 m at half depth on the 2 m grid in V16) with a dark core and fainter darkening around it out to about 150 m, on cratered plains 123 km N of Labeatis Mensa and 368 km NE of lead 45, in three CTX images on three orbits: N09 2020-08-16, U10 2022-07-23 and V16 2024-12-20 (z -8.4, -5.7 and -16.3 on a 30 m disc). A small crater about 150 m E of the spot shows in all seven images. Absent in four earlier images (z -0.8 to -2.6; the close-ups show plain ground at the spot in all four): P12 2007-10-24 (r 0.73), D20 2014-01-27 (incidence 42.3 deg from azimuth 194 deg; r 0.82), J05 2016-07-16 (hazy, r 0.28) and J15 2017-05-27 under nearly the same sun as V16 (incidence 40.2 and 41.6 deg, azimuth 158 and 166 deg; r 0.67). N09 and U10 were taken under a low sun (incidence 69 and 67 deg). The registered before/after difference reaches z -2.6 at the spot (68 x 72 m at half depth), nearly as deep as the deepest change in the 2 km crop, which lies at its edge (z -2.7). A control feature 300 m E reads z -5.2 to -7.7 in every image, including J15 (-6.9), where the spot reads -0.8. Window 2017-05 to 2020-08; no image aimed at an impact; HiRISE ESP_026180_2080 (2012-02-26, of a small chaos patch) covers the site, before the spot formed; the nearest catalogued new impact is 121 km away (a CTX candidate site that formed between 2014-01 and 2023-03), a separate event; no MOC coverage; 136 deg from InSight.
alternatives: a dust devil that stalled (unlikely: the spot is compact, has no tracks near it and lasted at least 4.3 years); dark material shed from the nearby crater (nothing changed at the crater); the 2020 and 2022 images were taken under a low sun, but the 2024 image, under the 2017 sun, shows the spot clearly

name: plains 272 km SE of Apollinaris Sulci
size_m: ~40x25 dark head (42x26) at the WNW end of a fainter tail 73 m long
evidence: Elongated dark spot: a dark head about 40 x 25 m (42 x 26 m at half depth on the 2 m grid in V22) at the WNW end of a fainter tail (73 x 38 m at a quarter of the depth), on smooth plains 272 km SE of Apollinaris Sulci and 525 km S of lead 83, about 200 m W of a small crater that shows in all four images, in two CTX images on two orbits: V22 2025-06-10 and W01 2025-08-21 (z -7.9 and -6.4 on a 25 m disc). Absent in two earlier images, both aligned (z +0.1 and -0.3): B18 2010-02-11 (incidence 55.9 deg; r 0.75) and U20 2023-05-26 under the same sun as V22 (incidence 62.3 and 63.6 deg, azimuth 224 deg in both; r 0.80). The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (60 x 52 m at half depth, z -1.95), the deepest change anywhere in the 2 km crop at the finer smoothing. The control is not informative (a feature 300 m W reads only z -0.4 to -0.9 in every image). Window 2023-05 to 2025-06; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 33.5 km); the nearest new-impact-like target is a HiRISE 'New dark deposit near Medusae Fossae' (2024-05-23) 99.5 km away, and the nearest CTX candidate impact site is 143 km away; no MOC coverage. It lies 49.0 deg from InSight, just inside the area of Bickel et al. (2025), but it formed after May 2023, after that catalogue's period (2018-2022).
alternatives: a dark deposit left by wind or a stalled dust devil (possible for the elongated shape; no tracks in the 2 km crop, and HiRISE targeted a 'new dark deposit' 100 km away in 2024); an image defect is excluded by the second image, taken on another orbit 72 days later; an oblique impact can also make an elongated dark zone

name: Amazonis Planitia, 272 km SW of Qara crater
evidence: Compact dark spot about 36 m across (28 x 50 m at half depth on the 2 m grid) on smooth plains in Amazonis Planitia, 272 km SW of Qara crater and 173 km from lead 38, about 400 m W of the edge of a rough knobby unit, in two orbits: U16 2023-01-08 (z -5.4 on a 20 m disc) and V15 2024-11-11 (z -8.9). Absent in three aligned earlier images (z -1.5 to +0.5): B19 2010-03-27 (r 0.46 to 0.55), G01 2010-07-10 (r 0.38 to 0.48) and K01 2018-01-21 (r 0.61 to 0.66), all under a sun 5 to 9 deg lower (incidence 44 to 48 vs 39 deg); the small craters 40 m W of the spot show in all five images. The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot within 100 m (z -1.5, 44 x 68 m at half depth); deeper minima lie only at the crop's edge, 1.2 to 1.4 km away. The control feature 300 m ENE is only faint in the earlier images (z -0.8 to -1.4), so it does not test their detectability. Window 2018-01 to 2023-01; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 43.1 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 48.6 km away (a CTX-targeted site that formed between 2008 and 2010), a separate and older event; no MOC coverage; 69 deg from InSight.
alternatives: a dust devil that stalled (no tracks in the 2 km crop, and the spot is unchanged after 22 months); dark material in a small pre-existing hollow (none in the earlier images, whose lower sun would show a hollow better); a slope streak (the spot is on flat plains, 400 m from the nearest slope)

name: plains 276 km NE of Tharsis Tholus
size_m: ~69 (58x114), a darker core in a diffuse zone elongated N-S
evidence: Diffuse dark spot about 70 m across (58 x 114 m at half depth, elongated N-S) with a darker core, on lava plains 276 km NE of Tharsis Tholus and 67 km from lead 54, in two orbits: N07 2020-06-25 under a low sun (incidence 63 deg; z -4.3 on a 35 m disc) and V18 2025-02-22 (z -4.4). Absent in B18 2010-02-19 under almost the same sun as V18 (incidence 41.9 vs 42.8 deg, azimuth 198 vs 196 deg; r 0.45 to 0.58; z 0.0); P11 2007-09-12 is blank at the site (r 0.03) and not counted. A control feature 260 m WSW reads z -2.4 in B18, where the spot reads 0.0. The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot within 100 m (z -1.9, 92 x 108 m at half depth); the only deeper change is at the crop's edge, 1.3 km away. Window 2010-02 to 2020-06, unfaded 4.7 years later; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 40.8 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 73.5 km away (a site targeted by HiRISE and CTX in 2024, which formed between 2008 and 2020), a separate event; no MOC coverage; 134 deg from InSight.
alternatives: a newly darkened stretch of a pre-existing dark band 100 to 150 m SW that runs the same way as the spot's long axis (dust sliding in a shallow fissure, or wind scour along it); a dust devil that stalled (no tracks, and unchanged after 4.7 years); only one usable earlier image

name: Elysium Planitia, west of Albor Tholus
size_m: 25-30, plus a new companion 195 m NNW
evidence: Compact dark spot on lava plains W of Albor Tholus, identical in 4 images 2025-04 to 2025-11 (z -9.0, -8.4, -9.0, -7.5); absent 2014-05 (same sun, r 0.67) and 2022-07 (r 0.34). A fainter companion 195 m NNW is new too (z -0.6, -0.5 before; -3.2 to -6.4 after): a small cluster. Two epochs aligned by masked template matching. Nearby HiRISE 'Fresh impact crater' (12.4 km) and CTX April-July 2025 candidate (23.7 km) are different sites.
alternatives: dust devil or wind streak (rejected: compact, stable 7 months); misregistration (rejected: surrounding craters line up)

name: knobby plains near Mangala Fossa
size_m: ~40 (44x42 in K22), a darker core in a soft halo
evidence: A dark spot about 40 m across (44 x 42 m at half depth in K22) with a darker core in a soft halo, on a smooth patch among low knobs on the knobby plains near Mangala Fossa, 540 km from lead 97, in two CTX images on two orbits: K22 2019-10-24 and V17 2025-01-07 (z -7.4 and -6.6 on a 15 m disc). Absent in B20 2010-04-30 under the same sun as K22 (incidence 63.2 vs 64.4 deg, azimuth 227 deg in both; r 0.70 to 0.78; z +0.4) and in F05 2014-08-03 (r 0.51 to 0.60; z +0.6). A pre-existing control feature 280 m NNE reads z -3.5 and -2.6 in those two images, and the knob shadows 40 to 100 m from the spot are the same in B20 and K22, so a pit or knob at the spot would have shown in 2010. The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (z -1.9, 52 x 64 m at half depth), the deepest change anywhere in the 2 km crop. Window 2014-08 to 2019-10; still visible 5.2 years later. No image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 28.8 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 56 km away (a young impact site imaged by HiRISE in 2013 that formed between 2006 and 2008), a separate event; no MOC coverage; 79.3 deg from InSight, outside the Bickel et al. (2025) area. The verification position was 38 m off the spot's centre; the lead position is re-centred on it.
alternatives: a dust devil that stalled (no tracks in a 5 km window, and the spot lasted over 5 years); dark sand gathered in a small hollow (no hollow shows in 2010 under the same sun); a defect in B20, whose one-column line passes 70 m W of the spot (F05 shows nothing either)

name: plains of the Nepenthes Mensae region, 408 km W of InSight
size_m: ~120 halo (112x128 in V14) around a dark core ~40
evidence: A new dark spot, a dark core about 40 m across in a halo about 120 m wide (112 x 128 m at half depth in V14), on plains of the Nepenthes Mensae region 408 km W of the InSight lander, in two CTX images on two orbits: U19 2023-04-18 and V14 2024-10-06 (z -4.8 and -4.7 on a 20 m disc). Absent in J06 2016-08-14 (r 0.37 to 0.45; z -0.1) and K21 2019-09-16, under almost the same sun as U19 (incidence 48.8 vs 48.2 deg, azimuth 216 vs 209 deg; r 0.31 to 0.35; z +1.2). A pre-existing control feature 190 m NNE reads z -5.7 and -3.1 in J06 and K21, so both would have shown a spot this dark. The spot is real image data (a smooth dip, about 5% darker at its centre in V14, with no missing pixels). The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot at both smoothings (z -2.2 and -1.9, 108 x 124 m at half depth), the deepest change anywhere in the 2 km crop, and a 5 x 5 km registered window shows no other new dark mark and no tracks. Window 2019-09 to 2023-04; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 30 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 110 km away (a Daubar et al. 2022 cluster that formed between 2016-09 and 2020-08), a separate event; no MOC coverage; 6.9 deg from InSight, inside the area of Bickel et al. (2025) and possibly its period, whose entries all have HiRISE images, while none covers this spot.
alternatives: a dust devil that stalled (no tracks in the 5 km window, and the spot has a compact core); an image defect (two images on two orbits show it at the same place); low alignment of the two earlier images (r 0.31 to 0.45, against the striped V14; U19, with the spot, scores 0.39), though the control feature and the craters around the spot line up in both

name: etched plains of Arabia Terra near Indus Vallis
size_m: ~75 (110x86 in V16), a dark core with ragged edges

(2025) area.
alternatives: a patch where wind stripped bright dust (the spot has a darker core and appeared within 17 months with nothing else changing in the 5 km window); a dust devil that stalled (no tracks); a slope streak on the etched ridges (the spot is not drawn out downslope)

name: cluster on the plains of west-central Arabia Terra
size_m: a cluster of at least six spots within ~350 m, the largest ~40 (40x44 in U22)
evidence: A new cluster of at least six dark spots within about 350 m, the largest about 40 m across (40 x 44 m at half depth in U22, 6% darker than its surroundings), on the plains of west-central Arabia Terra, 197 km from leads 57 and 72, in two CTX images on two orbits: U18 2023-03-27 and U22 2023-07-10 (z -10.9 and -9.6 on a 20 m disc). The spots are real image data (smooth dips with no missing pixels). The registered before/after difference is deepest at the largest spot at both smoothings (z -5.0 and -3.2, 48 x 52 m at half depth), the deepest change anywhere in the 2 km crop, and a 5 x 5 km registered window shows no other new dark mark and no tracks. Window 2014-04 to 2023-03; no image aimed at an impact (U18 was taken with HiRISE ESP_078121_2025, which ends 43 km away); no HiRISE of the spot (nearest edge 41 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 47 km away (a site HiRISE monitored in 2022, probably the 24.5 m crater of Daubar et al. 2022, 48 km away, which formed between 2001 and 2003), a separate event; leads 57 and 72 formed in an overlapping window but 197 km away, too far for one impact; no MOC coverage; 116.4 deg from InSight, outside the Bickel et al. (2025) area.
alternatives: a dust devil that stalled (no tracks, and a cluster of separate round spots is not a dust-devil pattern); a change in shading (F01 and U22 have almost the same sun); the control feature is dark only in F01, so the detectability test is weaker than usual

(2025) and possibly its period, whose entries all have HiRISE images, while none covers this spot.

name: cratered plains of northern Arabia Terra, SE of Quenisset crater
size_m: ~40 (38x54 in U21), compact, with a smaller new spot 154 m SSW
impact_targeted_images: K05_055133_2149 is itself targeted at another candidate impact (2012-2018) 120.6 km away
evidence: A new compact dark spot about 40 m across (38 x 54 m at half depth in U21, 5% darker than its surroundings), with a smaller new dark spot 154 m SSW and possibly a fainter third about 220 m WSW, on cratered plains of northern Arabia Terra 107 km SE of Quenisset crater, 141 km from lead 44, in three CTX images on three orbits: U18 2023-03-22, U21 2023-06-18 and V17 2025-01-07 (z -16.1, -9.0 and -14.9 on a 20 m disc). (2022) that formed between 2010-11 and 2015-10, before this window opened), a separate event; lead 44 formed in an overlapping window but 141 km away, too far for one impact; no MOC coverage; 90.0 deg from InSight, outside the Bickel et al. (2025) area.

name: plains in south-eastern Gordii Fossae
size_m: ~60 head with a ~140 m E tail (196x96 in J04), fading (38x46 in V07)
impact_targeted_images: K15_059399_1941 is itself targeted at another candidate impact (2016-2018) 21.6 km away
evidence: A new dark spot, a head about 60 m across with a tail about 140 m long to the E (196 x 96 m at half depth in J04, 5% darker than its surroundings) and a bright arc on its W side that appears with it, on plains in south-eastern Gordii Fossae, 117 km SE of the centre of that feature and 114 km from lead 6, in three CTX images on three orbits: J04 2016-06-08, K15 2019-03-29 and V07 2024-03-29 (z -6.1, -3.9 and -8.3 on a 30 m disc); by 2024 it has faded to a 38 x 46 m core 2% darker than its surroundings. (2025) area.

(2025) area.

name: south of Acheron Fossae

evidence: Compact round dark spot on lava plains 13 km WNW of L11, unchanged in 7 images 2022-07 to 2025-09 (z -5.8 to -16.1) under 45-59 deg sun and 141-203 deg azimuth; absent 2014-05 (z +0.65, r 0.64) under the same sun as 2025-08, while a shadow 92 m away reads z -2.1. Found by hand; the filter rules that rejected it were corrected.
alternatives: shadow (rejected: absent at the same sun, present at every sun since); could be in Bickel et al. 2025 (site and window qualify) but no HiRISE image of it exists

name: knobby plains in southern Arabia Terra, 167 km SE of Janssen crater
evidence: A new compact dark spot about 50 m across, in two lobes (34 x 66 m at half depth in U11, 5% darker than its surroundings; its darkest raw pixels 105 against a local median of 112, 12% less light with the square-root encoding undone), on knobby plains in southern Arabia Terra, 167 km SE of Janssen crater (268 km from lead 61, the nearest lead), in two CTX images from two orbits: U11 2022-08-14 (z -10.5 on a 20 m disc) and U16 2023-01-29 (7.8 deg off nadir, r 0.32; z -6.3). Absent in G07 2011-01-14 (r 0.73; z +0.2) and N10 2020-09-22 (r 0.73; z +0.6), which show only the knobby texture at the place. N10 has almost the same sun as U11 (incidence 49.9 against 47.5 deg, azimuth 151 against 150 deg), and U16, under a sun 45 deg away in direction (azimuth 195 deg) and 6 deg higher, still shows the spot, so it is not shading; it formed between 2020-09-22 and 2022-08-14. A dark feature 300 m ENE reads z -2.1 in N10 (-1.7 in G07) while the spot's place reads +0.6 and +0.2 (the control check, passed). With brightness trends wider than about 200 m removed, the registered difference of N10 with U11 is deepest at the spot at the finer smoothing (z -2.3 against -1.8 for the next deepest minimum) and level with the next at the coarser one (-1.5 against -1.5); the difference of G07 and N10 with U11 and U16 is deepest 960 m W, on a large slope at the crop's west edge whose shading changes under U16's sun, and second at the spot (-1.9 against -2.0). Registered 5 x 5 km windows with those trends removed show no other new compact dark mark and no tracks. U10 2022-07-28, 17 days before U11, could not be aligned (r 0.0, and no match within 3.5 km), so it is not used. Window 2020-09 to 2022-08; no image aimed at it (G07 was aimed at clusters of buttes seen in THEMIS images, the others are regional images of Arabia Terra); no HiRISE of the spot (the nearest edge, 53.0 km, is that of ESP_083553_1805, 2024, a terrain sample); the nearest HiRISE image aimed at a candidate impact site, ESP_069760_1795 (2021-06-14), is 75.5 km away, and the CTX image taken with it, N19_069760_1797, was aimed at the same site, which formed between 2019-08 and 2021-05; the nearest entry in Daubar et al. (2022), a cluster with a 3.2 m largest crater that formed between 2005-07 and 2015-07, is 81.7 km away; no MOC coverage; 95.8 deg from InSight, outside the Bickel et al. (2025) area.
alternatives: shading of a knob (N10 has almost the same sun as U11 and shows nothing, and U16 shows the spot under a sun 45 deg away in direction); an image defect (two images from two orbits, although both are striped); a dust devil (no tracks in the 5 km windows, and the spot is still there 5.5 months later); dark material moved by wind among the knobs (possible, but the spot is compact and appeared on open ground between knobs); only two images show it, U16 is poorly aligned (r 0.32), the four-image difference is deepest elsewhere (at a slope whose shading changes), and the window is 23 months long; a compact dark spot appearing on dusty plains and lasting is the usual look of a small new impact

name: wind-streaked plains on south-eastern Amazonis Mensa, 113 km SW of Amazonis Sulci
evidence: A new dark spot with a dark halo, the look of a fresh impact blast zone: a dark core about 150 m across (78 x 148 m at half depth in U04; 7% less light than the plains outside the halo, with the square-root encoding undone) with short dark arms and a chain of smaller dark blobs reaching about 250 m to the east, inside a diffuse dark halo about 650 m across (at least 2% less light out to about 325 m from the centre), on wind-streaked plains of the Medusae Fossae Formation on south-eastern Amazonis Mensa, 113 km SW of Amazonis Sulci (224 km from lead 20, the nearest lead), in two CTX images from two orbits: U04 2022-01-18 (8.8 deg off nadir; z -4.0 on a 60 m disc) and U14 2022-11-12 (27.2 deg off nadir, under a sun 24 deg higher; r 0.17; z -2.3), which shows the same core, arms, eastern blobs and halo; U14's map position is 1.7 km off and was found by wide registration (+1697 m E, +248 m N). Absent in the only earlier image, B01 2008-09-01 (r 0.35; z -0.2; no darkening at the place), which has nearly the same sun as U04 (incidence 57.6 against 57.0 deg, azimuth 215 against 199 deg); it formed between 2008-09-01 and 2022-01-18. The nearest dark feature in B01, 232 m N, reads only z -0.4, so the control check is not informative. With brightness trends wider than about 200 m removed, the registered difference of B01 with U04 is deepest at the spot at the coarser smoothing (z -2.8 against -2.3 for the next deepest minimum) and second at the finer one (-3.2 against -4.1); the deeper minimum is the shaded inside of a small crater 980 m NE that is in both images, under suns 16 deg apart in direction; with U14 added the spot is second to that crater at both (-2.2 against -4.4; -2.0 against -2.5). Registered 5 x 5 km windows with those trends removed show no other new dark mark and no tracks. Window 2008-09 to 2022-01; no image aimed at it (B01 was aimed at a scarp and valleys south of Amazonis Sulci, U04 is a regional image of Amazonis Mensa, and U14 rode along with HiRISE ESP_076386_1760, of eolian erosion of the Medusae Fossae Formation, whose edge is 45.8 km away); no HiRISE of the spot (the nearest edge, 41.5 km, is that of ESP_035479_1780, 2014, a terrain sample of the Medusae Fossae Formation); the nearest HiRISE image aimed at a candidate impact site, ESP_089612_1780 (2025-09-07), is 150.0 km away, and the CTX image taken with it, W02_089612_1780, was aimed at the same site, which formed between 2019-07 and 2025-03; the nearest entry in Daubar et al. (2022), a cluster with a 9.3 m largest crater that formed between 2003-06 and 2008-08, is 171.6 km away; no MOC coverage; 79.2 deg from InSight, outside the Bickel et al. (2025) area.
alternatives: a dust devil or a wind-made dark patch (the arms, the chain of blobs and the halo around a dark core are the pattern of an impact blast, not of a dust-devil track, and the spot is unchanged ten months later); shading (B01 has nearly the same sun as U04 and shows nothing, U14 shows the spot under a sun 24 deg higher, and the plains are flat); an image defect (two images from two orbits, seen from different directions); only one earlier image, a window thirteen years long, and U14 is poorly aligned (r 0.17), although the spot is unmistakable in it; a dark core with rays and a halo appearing on dusty plains is the usual look of a new impact or cluster

name: plains east of Licus Vallis, 93 km E of its centre
evidence: A new compact dark spot about 25 m across (24 x 32 m at half depth in U20, 6% darker; its darkest raw pixels 87 against a local median of 93, 13% less light with the square-root encoding undone) on cratered plains east of Licus Vallis, 93 km E of the valley's centre (215 km from lead 159, the nearest lead), in two CTX images from two orbits: U20 2023-05-21 (the discovery image; z -8.4 on a 20 m disc) and W03 2025-10-16 (r 0.52; z -4.3), where it is fainter. Absent in five earlier images: P18 2008-04-20 (r 0.80; z +1.2), P19 2008-05-01 (r 0.71; z +0.2), N09 2020-08-06 (r 0.28; z -0.0), N13 2020-12-18 (r 0.39; z -0.3) and N15 2021-02-13 (r 0.39; z -0.1). P18 has the same sun as U20 (incidence 52.3 against 54.4 deg, azimuth 218 against 218 deg), so it is not shading. U03 2021-12-20, hazy and not aligned (r -0.01), is not used. It formed between 2021-02-13 and 2023-05-21. Control passed: a dark feature 220 m SW reads z -4.7 in P18 while the spot's place reads +1.2. With brightness trends wider than about 200 m removed, the registered difference of P18 with U20 does not single the spot out: it is second at the finer smoothing (z -2.0 against -2.1 at a textured place 570 m SE that is already dark in 2008, candidate U20_078829_1784_r03) and fifth at the coarser one, which blurs a spot this small; with all five earlier images against both later ones it is second at the finer smoothing (-1.2 against -1.4 at the same place). Registered 5 x 5 km windows show no tracks. Window 2021-02 to 2023-05; no image aimed at it (all are regional images of the terrain east of Licus Vallis; P18 rode along with HiRISE PSP_008121_1780, of valleys in an impact crater floor, whose edge is 32.0 km away); no HiRISE of the spot (the nearest edge, 6.3 km, is that of ESP_046467_1765, 2016); the nearest HiRISE image aimed at a candidate impact site, ESP_068081_1755 (2021-02-03), is 107.8 km away, and the CTX image taken with it, N15_068081_1757, aimed at the same site, which formed between 2014-07 and 2016-08, 110.0 km; the nearest entry in Daubar et al. (2022), a cluster with a 24.0 m largest crater that formed between 2007-05 and 2013-06, is 303.2 km away; no MOC coverage; 10.5 deg from InSight, inside the Bickel et al. (2025) area, with a window overlapping its 2018-2022 period, but no HiRISE image covers it, so very probably not in that catalogue.
alternatives: a dust devil (a compact spot, no tracks, and it lasts at least 29 months); shading (P18 has the same sun as U20 and shows nothing, on flat plains); an image defect (two images from two orbits); a small spot, only 4 to 6 pixels across, which the filtered difference does not single out, and the later image shows it fainter; a compact new dark spot on dusty plains is the usual look of a new small impact

name: wind-ridged plains in Daedalia Planum, 299 km E of Arimanes Rupes
evidence: A new compact dark spot about 35 m across (52 x 38 m at half depth in V08, 3% darker; 4% less light at its core) on wind-ridged plains in Daedalia Planum, 299 km E of Arimanes Rupes (282 km from lead 20, the nearest lead), in three CTX images from three orbits: V08 2024-04-06 (the discovery image; z -5.5 on a 20 m disc), V15 2024-11-02 (r 0.08; z -7.0) and V17 2025-01-08 (r -0.01; z -11.7). V15 is blurred and V17 noisy, so their alignment scores are low, but both show the spot at the same place among the ridges. Absent in both earlier images: P06 2007-04-16 (r 0.49; z +0.1) and P14 2007-12-20 (r 0.26; z -0.9). P06 has the same sun as V08 (incidence 53.0 against 53.8 deg, azimuth 175 against 170 deg), so it is not shading. It formed between 2007-12-20 and 2024-04-06. Control not informative: the nearest dark feature, 290 m NE, reads only -1.3 and -0.3 in the earlier images. With brightness trends wider than about 200 m removed, the registered difference of the same-sun pair P06 and V08 has its only minimum below -1.0 at the spot at the finer smoothing (z -1.2) and none at the coarser; with all images it is second at the finer smoothing (-1.6 against -1.7 at a place 1.0 km ENE) and not first at the coarser, where the poorly aligned later images add noise. Window 2007-12 to 2024-04; no image aimed at it (P06 and P14 are images of craters with wind streaks, V08 and V17 regional images; V15 rode along with HiRISE ESP_085643_1690, aimed at a candidate recent impact site 15.6 km away, whose edge is 10.3 km from the spot); no HiRISE of the spot and no MOC coverage. The CTX image aimed at that candidate site, V13_085155_1688 (2024-09-25, 18.7 km; formed between 2018-04 and 2024-04), does not cover this spot, so the camera team's site is a different one, although their search of V08 may have passed over this spot too. The nearest entry in Daubar et al. (2022), a single 1.6 m crater that formed between 2008-07 and 2016-06, is 83.1 km away; 82.7 deg from InSight, outside the Bickel et al. (2025) area.
alternatives: shading (P06 has the same sun as V08 and shows nothing, on low ridged plains); an image defect (three images from three orbits); a dust devil (a compact spot lasting at least nine months); the later images are poorly aligned by the score and the control is not informative, but a compact new dark spot on dusty plains is the usual look of a new small impact

name: lava plains 350 km SE of Fesenkov crater, 412 km NE of Tharsis Tholus
evidence: A new compact dark spot about 40 m across (46 x 38 m at half depth in U09, 4% darker; 5% less light at its core, 8% in V17) on lava plains 350 km SE of Fesenkov crater and 412 km NE of Tharsis Tholus (118 km from lead 54, the nearest lead), in two CTX images from two orbits: U09 2022-06-12 (the discovery image; z -6.5 on a 20 m disc) and V17 2025-01-04 (r 0.50; z -10.5). Absent in both earlier images: K15 2019-03-05 (r 0.67; z -0.2) and N06 2020-05-30 (r 0.67; z -0.2). N06 has nearly the same sun as U09 (incidence 62.5 against 63.4 deg, azimuth 163 against 150 deg) and K15 a sun like V17's (incidence 37.1 against 40.2 deg), so it is not shading. It formed between 2020-05-30 and 2022-06-12. Control passed: a dark feature 200 m SSW reads z -2.2 in N06 and -1.8 in K15 while the spot's place reads -0.2. With brightness trends wider than about 200 m removed, the registered difference of the earlier with the later images is deepest at the spot at the finer smoothing (z -2.7) and level with a place 1.1 km ENE at the coarser (-1.9 against -1.9); for the same-sun pair N06 and U09 alone it is deepest at the coarser smoothing and second at the finer, behind a place near a small crater 790 m ENE whose shading changes with the 13 deg shift in sun azimuth (-2.5 against -2.7). Window 2020-05 to 2022-06; no image aimed at it (regional images of the plains NE of Tharsis Tholus and SE of Fesenkov crater; U09 rode along with HiRISE ESP_074419_1970, of landforms SE of Fesenkov crater, whose edge is 19.8 km from the spot); P16 2008-02-21 was not verified and P19 2008-05-31 carries an error flag, so neither is used; no HiRISE of the spot and no MOC coverage; the nearest HiRISE image aimed at a candidate impact site, ESP_092708_1960 (2026-05-07), is 104.8 km away, and the CTX image taken with it, W10_092708_1958, was aimed at the same site, which formed between 2012-09 and 2024-10; the nearest entry in Daubar et al. (2022), a cluster with a 16.9 m largest crater that formed between 2004-02 and 2006-02, is 147.8 km away; 135.5 deg from InSight, outside the Bickel et al. (2025) area.
alternatives: shading (N06 has nearly the same sun as U09 and shows nothing, on flat lava plains); an image defect (two images from two orbits); a dust devil (a compact spot lasting at least 31 months, darker in 2025 than in 2022); volcanic dark fallout, as proposed for a fissure near Tharsis Tholus 459 km away (a 40 m spot that appeared within two years is far smaller and quicker); a compact new dark spot on dusty plains is the usual look of a new small impact

name: 'giant lobe' north of Pavonis Mons
impact_targeted_images: G12_022964_1845 covers the point but targets a 2010-2011 impact 19.9 km away
evidence: Compact dark spot on the 'giant lobe' N of Pavonis Mons, in 4 images 2025-03-10 to 2026-01-31 (z -9.3, -9.0, -6.5, -5.6, slowly fading); absent in 6 images 2019-09 to 2024-09-26 (r 0.51-0.78, incidence 37-58 deg) while a dark feature 250 m away reads z -2.3 to -3.8 in each. Formed within 165 days. 34 CTX images cover the site (monitoring).
alternatives: shadow (rejected: absent at every sun 2019-2024, present at every sun after); artefact (rejected: 4 images from 4 orbits)

name: Medusae Fossae Formation, south of Amazonis Mensa
evidence: Compact, slightly elongated dark spot on wind-streaked Medusae Fossae Formation S of Amazonis Mensa, z -5.5 (2025-07-31) and -4.2 (2025-11-07); absent 2008-08 and 2012-04 under the same sun (57-58 vs 59-60 deg; r 0.24, 0.38) while a dark feature 300 m away reads z -2.5 in 2012. The 2018 and 2022 images are featureless at the spot.
alternatives: wind exposure of darker substrate on friable yardang terrain (possible); 13-year window

name: terrain west of Cyane Fossae
size_m: 40-50 rayed dark zone around >= 3 craters of 2-3 m (HiRISE)
evidence: Black blob inside a 100 m hollow W of Cyane Fossae in W04_090389_2061 (2025-11-07, z -3.7) where the 2010-12-18 image (r 0.72) shows a bright, sunlit patch (z +0.8; a feature 280 m away reads -4.5). HiRISE from the same orbit resolves a radial dark pattern with rays in several directions around >= 3 dark ovals of 2-3 m with bright east rims: small craters lit from the west.
alternatives: dark slope streak (dust avalanche) on the hollow's wall (possible: such streaks occur in Cyane Fossae pits; argued against by the craters at its centre and rays pointing upslope; impacts can also trigger streaks); one before image only

name: north-west flank of Arsia Mons (cluster of dots)
impact_targeted_images: J08_047887_1728 covers the point but targets a 2012-2015 impact 36 km away
evidence: Cluster of 3-4 compact dark dots on bright plains of the NW flank of Arsia Mons, same pattern in 3 images 2025-01-23 to 2025-07-14 (main dot z -7.4, -8.1, -5.4); absent in 2008-09, 2015-12 and 2016-12 (r 0.57, 0.52, 0.31) under sun bracketing the later images (41-58 deg).
alternatives: none credible besides an impact cluster; detectability control weak (no comparable dark feature nearby)

name: floor of Cassini crater (Arabia Terra)
size_m: 80-100 core with a 200-300 m southward tail
evidence: Very dark round spot with a long southward tail on the flat floor of Cassini crater, present 2017-11-03 (z -7.0), 2023-10-21 (z -12.4) and 2026-02-08 (z -3.9, fading); absent 2008-04 and 2008-11 (r 0.53, 0.67; incidence 42 and 55 deg) while a dark feature 300 m away reads z -1.9 and -2.3.
alternatives: dark wind streak behind a small obstacle (unlikely: the core is round and new); slope streak (rejected: flat crater floor)

name: Arabia Terra, north of Schiaparelli crater
evidence: Compact dark spot on flat bright plains of Arabia Terra in two images from different orbits, 2024-09-07 (z -4.3, sun azimuth 153 deg) and 2025-07-13 (z -10.0, 210 deg), so not a shadow; absent 2013-12-19 and 2023-10-10 (r 0.74, 0.80), the latter under the same sun (53.9 vs 51.6 deg, azimuth 203 vs 210). Window 11 months.
alternatives: detectability control not informative (no comparable dark feature within 300 m); the 2024 image is low in contrast

name: eastern Ulysses Fossae (Tharsis lava plains)
evidence: Compact dark spot on smooth Tharsis lava plains between N-S graben, in 5 images from 5 orbits 2024-03-19 to 2025-07-09 (z -4.4 to -6.9; sun azimuth 161 to 208 deg, so not a shadow); absent 2010-01-27 (r 0.79; incidence 42 deg vs 40 deg in the 2025-01-02 detection), when a pre-existing dark feature 192 m W is detected (z -2.55) and the spot reads +0.1, and absent 2019-03-19 (r 0.40). Window 2019-03 to 2024-03 (firmly 2010-01 to 2024-03: the 2019 image does not show the control).
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind around a tiny pre-existing pit (unlikely: no landform at the spot at r 0.79, compact and unchanged for 16 months); shadow (excluded: sun azimuth spans 47 deg)

name: Elysium Planitia, platy lava plains west of Athabasca Valles
evidence: Compact dark spot with a diffuse halo on platy lava plains W of Athabasca Valles, in 5 images from 5 orbits 2021-06-08 to 2026-05-03 (z -8.8, -11.1 and -8.8 in 2021-2025, -4.7 in 2026 as it fades; sun azimuth 146 to 211 deg, so not a shadow); absent 2008-08-25 (r 0.81) under the same sun (incidence 52 vs 53 deg, azimuth 209 vs 207 deg), when a dark feature 226 m SE reads z -3.1 and the spot +0.8. Window 2008-08 to 2021-06; the nearest catalogued impact is 107.5 km away.
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: round, no streak, same shape for 5 years); lava-plate texture (excluded: nothing at the spot at r 0.81 in 2008)

name: northern Arabia Terra, NW of Cassini crater
impact_targeted_images: B01_010155_2094 and the later images were taken for a 2003-2005 impact 9.3 km away (PSP_003958_2095)
evidence: Diffuse dark spot ~150 m across with a darker ~90 m core in northern Arabia Terra, in N09 2020-08-03, U09 2022-06-17 and V21 2025-05-22 (z -3.4, -4.1, -5.7 on a 45 m disc) and by eye in V19 2025-03-22, which registers ~600 m off and cannot be scored. Absent 2008-09-25 (r 0.37) under the same sun as V21 (incidence 49 vs 44 deg), when a control 116 m N reads z -2.4 and the spot -0.6; absent 2014-12-08 under the same sun as N09 (incidence 70 vs 72 deg, poorly aligned) and 2018-09-11 (during the global dust storm). Window 2014-12 to 2020-08 (2008-09 to 2020-08 if the poorly aligned 2014 image is set aside).
alternatives: wind-driven albedo change (less likely: round, with a darker core, and stable from 2020 to 2025); dust devil (no track in four images)

name: plains N of Arsia Mons, S of Biblis Patera
evidence: Compact dark spot (core ~60x45 m) on the plains N of Arsia Mons, S of Biblis Patera, in V17 2025-01-23 and V21 2025-05-25 (z -9.3, -7.2 on a 25 m disc; sun azimuth 211 and 220 deg); absent 2008-08-15 (r 0.84) under the same sun as V21 (incidence 58 vs 58 deg), 2008-10-14 and 2015-12-15 (r 0.45). A control 300 m NW reads z -2.1 to -2.7 in every image, earlier and later, while the spot reads +0.3 to +1.2 before. Window 2015-12 to 2025-01; the nearest catalogued impact is 28.0 km away (2008-2012).
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: compact, and nothing there in 2008 under the same sun); shadow (excluded by the same-sun 2008 image)

name: Arabia Terra (NW of Pasteur Crater)
evidence: Present in 3 CTX images 2025-02 to 2026-04 and resolved by HiRISE at 0.5 m/px: sharp dark patch with digitate margins and a 1-2 m dark point at its edge on flat dusty plains; absent 2010 under the same sun.
alternatives: wind-stripped dust patch (unlikely: compact, centred on a dark point)

name: Elysium Planitia (formed Sep-Dec 2023)
evidence: Compact dark spot (core ~55x75 m) on Elysium Planitia, in V04 2023-12-25 and V20 2025-04-25 (z -11.9, -10.6 on a 25 m disc); absent in four earlier images, 2012-06-03, 2020-05-03, 2021-12-07 and 2023-09-06 (r 0.59-0.67; the spot reads +0.1 to +0.5 while a control 220 m W reads -2.1 to -4.8). Window 2023-09-06 to 2023-12-25, 110 days; the nearest catalogued impact is 76 km away. Inside the InSight study area of Bickel et al. (2025), but formed after it.
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: compact, appeared within 110 days and unchanged for 16 months); shadow (excluded: four earlier images under similar suns)

name: Acheron Fossae region (dot beside a small crater)
evidence: Compact dark dot (core ~50 m) 70 m W of an old small crater in the Acheron Fossae region, in U19 2023-04-12, U21 2023-06-11 and V17 2025-01-28 (z -4.6, -2.9, -9.9 on a 20 m disc); absent 2012-01-08 under the same sun (incidence 39 vs 42 deg, azimuth 180 vs 181; r 0.36), when the spot reads -0.2 and a control 170 m SW -3.3. Window 2012-01 to 2023-04; the nearest catalogued impact is 23.6 km away and formed 2015-2023 (a different site).
alternatives: shadow of a small pre-existing crater (excluded: nothing there under the same sun in 2012, while the old crater beside it shows); dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: compact)

name: Daedalia Planum lava plains
evidence: Compact dark spot (core ~40 m) with a faint halo on Daedalia Planum lava plains, in K11 2018-11-30 and V22 2025-06-30 (z -5.4, -6.8 on a 20 m disc); absent 2007-11-24, 2007-12-21 and 2008-08-12, the last under the same sun as V22 (incidence 67 vs 67 deg, r 0.94); a control 170 m W reads -3.2 to -6.5 in those images while the spot reads -0.0 to +0.2. Window 2008-08 to 2018-11; the nearest catalogued impact is 83 km away.
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: compact and unchanged for 6.5 years); shadow (excluded by the same-sun 2008 image)

name: plains N of Tithonium Chasma
evidence: Compact dark spot (core ~30x35 m) just W of a small knob on the plains N of Tithonium Chasma, in V20 2025-04-16 and W08 2026-03-04 (z -17.4, -2.8 on a 15 m disc; W08 is poorly aligned by the score, r 0.10, but the knob and a crater 1 km SSW line up). The sun azimuths are 220 and 162 deg and the spot lies on the sunward side of the knob, so it is not its shadow. Absent 2008-09-17 under the same sun as V20 (incidence 57 vs 56 deg, r 0.34), when the spot reads +0.6 and a control 225 m ENE -5.4. Window 2008-09 to 2025-04; the nearest catalogued impacts, 19.2 km (2026) and 34.4 km (2023-2025), are different sites.
alternatives: shadow of the knob (excluded: sunward side, and absent under the same sun in 2008); dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: compact)

name: Cerberus plains (rayed dark spot)
evidence: Rayed dark spot (core of several blobs, radial fingers) on flat lava plains; identical in 4 images 2023-10 to 2025-11, absent 2010 under the same sun (54 vs 55-57 deg).
alternatives: wind-stripped dust patch (possible); slope streak on adjacent narrow fracture (unlikely); may be in the Bickel et al. 2025 InSight-era catalogue, which could not be downloaded (unlikely: every entry there has a HiRISE image, none covers this point)

name: bedform terrain W of Echus Chasma
evidence: Compact dark spot (core ~50 m) on rippled bedform terrain W of Echus Chasma, in U18 2023-03-29, V18 2025-02-12, V20 2025-04-13 and V23 2025-07-06 (z -9.8, -7.5, -8.7, -7.3 on a 20 m disc); absent 2007-04-06, 2012-03-23 and 2013-01-30 (r 0.34, 0.31, 0.13; z -0.6, +0.3, -0.7; the bedform crests line up in every image), the 2012 image under the same sun as V20 (incidence 50 vs 50 deg, azimuth 216 vs 214); a control 75 m SW reads -2.3, -2.7 and -1.5 in the early images. Window 2013-01 to 2023-03; the nearest catalogued impact is 59 km away.
alternatives: dark sand gathered between bedforms (unlikely: a round spot that has not moved in 2.3 years); shadow (excluded by the same-sun 2012 image)

name: southern Arabia Terra, E of Schiaparelli crater
evidence: Compact dark spot (core ~55x65 m) in southern Arabia Terra E of Schiaparelli crater, in U20 2023-05-01 and V18 2025-02-17 (z -10.4, -14.7 on a 22 m disc); absent 2010-09-06 under the same sun (incidence 55 vs 53 deg, azimuth 206 vs 216; r 0.61, z -0.0). Window 2010-09 to 2023-05; the nearest catalogued impact is 89 km away.
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: compact, very dark, unchanged for 21 months); shadow (excluded by the same-sun 2010 image)

name: plains W of Uranius Mons (between Uranius Tholus and Uranius Mons)
evidence: Compact, very dark spot (core ~35x30 m) on the plains W of Uranius Mons, in N09 2020-08-12, V16 2024-12-05 and V18 2025-02-10 (z -8.2 and -19.1 on a 15 m disc in N09 and V16; -8.5, -10.4 and -10.8 on the band-pass map, which also scores V18, too uniform for the disc score); absent 2014-08-09 and 2016-05-12 (band-pass z +1.5, +1.4; r 0.38 and 0.25, with two small dark dots nearby lined up in every image), the 2016 image under a similar sun to V16 (incidence 48 vs 42 deg). Window 2016-05 to 2020-08; the nearest catalogued impact is 41.9 km away (formed 2007-2014, a different site).
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: compact and unchanged for 4.5 years); shadow (excluded: present under suns from 41 to 69 deg incidence)

name: plains NW of Echus Chasma
evidence: Compact dark spot (core ~55x45 m) with a diffuse halo among small knobs NW of Echus Chasma, in V17 2025-01-20 and V21 2025-05-05 (z -10.5, -9.1 on a 20 m disc); absent 2008-05-09 under the same sun as V21 (incidence 50 vs 51 deg, azimuth 214 vs 214; r 0.84), when the spot reads -1.0 and a control 300 m NE -5.7, with every knob lined up. Window 2008-05 to 2025-01; the nearest catalogued impact is 37.6 km away (2008-2010).
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: compact core with a halo); shadow (excluded by the same-sun 2008 image)

name: western Arabia Terra, ~700 km W of Pasteur crater
size_m: 40x46 dark patch around a ~2.5 m crater (HiRISE)
hirise: ESP_087470_1990 (2025-03-25, same orbit as V19, not impact-targeted)
evidence: Dark patch ~40 m across beside an older 80 m crater in western Arabia Terra, in U20 2023-05-04, V17 2025-01-06, V18 2025-02-03 and V19 2025-03-25 (z -5.9, -5.7, -5.2, -4.6 on a 20 m disc), with a dark band running ~70 m SSE along the older crater's west rim; absent 2010-02-17 and 2014-03-18 (z +0.0, +0.5; r 0.54, 0.82), the 2014 image under the same sun as U20 (incidence 47 vs 45 deg, azimuth 204 vs 200). HiRISE ESP_087470_1990, taken with V19 and catching the spot 1 km from its edge, resolves a crater ~2.5 m across at the centre of a 40 x 46 m dark patch, dark on its west wall and bright on its east wall as a pit lit from the WNW; HiRISE map position 19.1424 N 12.1889 E (the CTX and HiRISE map frames differ by ~370 m here). Window 2014-03 to 2023-05; the nearest catalogued impact is 187 km away; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: slope streak from the older crater's rim (argued against by the crater at the patch centre; the SSE band may be a small avalanche set off by the impact); a pre-existing small crater stripped of dust by wind or a dust devil (unlikely: round patch, no track)

name: central Ulysses Fossae (Tharsis lava plains beside a graben)
evidence: Compact, very dark spot (core ~45 m) on the smooth lava plains beside a graben in Ulysses Fossae, in U13 2022-10-09, U15 2022-12-02, V19 2025-03-20 and V21 2025-05-19 (z -11.7, -14.5, -22.4, -11.7 on an 18 m disc); absent 2010-04-30 under the same sun as V21 (incidence 48 vs 49 deg, azimuth 212 vs 211; r 0.60), when the spot reads +0.1 and a control 230 m SSE -6.1. Window 2010-04 to 2022-10; the nearest catalogued impact is 34.9 km away (formed 2010-2012, a different site); no MOC coverage.
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: compact and unchanged for 2.6 years under four different suns); shadow (excluded by the same-sun 2010 image)

name: Elysium Planitia near Cerberus Fossae, 190 km E of Zunil crater
evidence: Cluster of four or five dark blobs within ~120 x 100 m (the largest ~50 m) on the Elysium Planitia plains 190 km E of Zunil crater, in V20 2025-04-14 and V23 2025-07-06 (z -7.0, -6.7 on a 25 m disc); absent 2014-04-23, 2016-02-06, 2021-04-14 and 2023-01-28 (r 0.45-0.63; z -1.3, -1.6 and -1.2 in the 2014, 2021 and 2023 images, the 2016 one too noisy to score), the 2021 image under the same incidence as V20 (48 vs 49 deg, azimuth 198 vs 211), with the small dark features around the cluster lined up. Window 2023-01 to 2025-04, after the end of InSight's mission, and no HiRISE image covers it, so it cannot be in the InSight-era HiRISE-confirmed list of Bickel et al. 2025; the nearest catalogued impact is 50.7 km away (a HiRISE-targeted 2024 candidate, a different site); no MOC coverage.
alternatives: dark patches exposed by wind (unlikely: several compact blobs appearing together); dust devil (no track); several blobs appearing at once is the usual signature of an impactor that broke up in the atmosphere

name: smooth plains at the western rim of Echus Chasma
evidence: Compact, very dark spot (~47 m; 60 x 50 m in 2025, larger and darker in 2023) on the smooth plains 2 km W of the rim of Echus Chasma, in U18 2023-03-29 and V18 2025-02-12 (z -17.5, -8.6 on a 25 m disc; two orbits under the same sun; fading); absent 2006-12-22, 2012-10-12 and 2016-07-25 (z -0.1, -0.4, -0.2; r 0.67, 0.40, 0.56) under suns 6-9 deg lower, the 2006 one from nearly the same azimuth (199 vs 206 deg). No comparable dark feature nearby for a control (the nearest reads -0.4 to -2.0). Window 2016-07 to 2023-03; the nearest catalogued impact is 58.7 km away (a 2020 HiRISE candidate, a different site); the nearest HiRISE image (ESP_046857_1825, 2016, before the spot formed) ends 3.3 km away; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: dark material shed from the chasma wall (no: the spot is on level ground 2 km from the rim, and the wall's slope streaks are long and thin); dust devil (no track; a compact spot fading over two years is the usual look of a fresh blast zone); shadow (excluded: three earlier images under similar suns show nothing)

name: rippled plains 212 km SW of Biblis Tholus
evidence: Compact dark spot (~26 m; 30 x 28 m) on wind-rippled lava plains 212 km SW of Biblis Tholus, in U22 2023-07-14 and V20 2025-04-21 (z -12.8, -11.9 on a 15 m disc; two orbits under the same sun); absent 2012-05-30 under an identical sun (incidence 53.4 vs 53.1 deg, azimuth 215 vs 217; r 0.71), when the spot reads +0.2 and a control 220 m W -3.6. The 2011-04-18 image (G10) is featureless at the site (r 0.02) and is not counted. Window 2012-05 to 2023-07; the nearest catalogued impact is 27.4 km away (a CTX candidate formed 2013-2016, a different site); no MOC coverage.
alternatives: dark sand gathered between ripples (unlikely: round and isolated on a plain of uniform ripples, unchanged for 21 months); dust devil (no track); shadow (excluded by the identical-sun 2012 image)

name: cratered plains in the Memnonia region, 430 km E of Memnonia Sulci
evidence: Compact, dark round spot (~34 m; 34 x 36 m) on the cratered plains of the Memnonia region, 430 km E of Memnonia Sulci, in U19 2023-04-03 and V18 2025-02-16 (z -5.1, -6.8 on an 18 m disc; two orbits under the same sun, incidence 55 and 54 deg, azimuth 219); absent 2010-03-02, 2011-11-27 and 2014-01-29 (z +0.5, +0.6, -0.1; r 0.56, 0.35, 0.61), the 2010 and 2014 images under a similar sun (incidence 56 and 58 deg, azimuth 223), when a control 200 m WNW reads -2.7, -2.8, -3.4. A 2007-08-10 image (P10, during the global dust storm) and a 2018-12-16 image (K12) are too poorly aligned to decide (r 0.03, 0.05) and are not counted; a small crater 100 m S shows in both the 2010 and the 2025 image. Window 2014-01 to 2023-04; the nearest catalogued impact is 56.0 km away (a 2010-2016 cluster in Daubar et al. 2022, a different site); no MOC coverage.
alternatives: dust-devil scour (unlikely: round and compact, no track, still there 22 months later); dark sand patch (unlikely: isolated on a plain with no other dark patches); shadow (excluded by the similar-sun 2010 and 2014 images)

name: northern edge of Phison Patera, 220 km S of Rudaux crater
evidence: Compact, very dark round spot (~42 m; 42 x 44 m) on the plains at the northern edge of Phison Patera in Arabia Terra, 220 km S of Rudaux crater, in V15 2024-11-09 and V17 2025-01-31 (z -7.8, -9.1 on a 21 m disc; two orbits, the first under a sun from another azimuth, 147 vs 172 deg, and poorly aligned, r 0.25); absent in four images, 2014-05-14, 2019-07-03, 2021-09-08 and 2023-06-25 (z -0.1, +0.3, -0.4, -0.4; r 0.61, 0.81, 0.65, 0.81), the last under a sun like V17's (incidence 44 vs 43 deg, azimuth 189 vs 172), when a control 300 m ENE reads -1.6 to -2.5. A 250 m crater lies 600 m ESE. Window 2023-06 to 2024-11 (16.5 months); the nearest catalogued impact is 61.1 km away (a CTX candidate formed 2016-2021, a different site); HiRISE ESP_086796_2150, taken with V17, ends 24 km away; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: dust-devil scour (unlikely: compact and round, no track); dark material exposed by wind (unlikely: appeared within 16 months on ground unchanged for the nine years before); shadow (excluded by the similar-sun 2023 image)

name: plains among the Erebus Montes
size_m: diffuse ~70 (74x130 in CTX, 72x90 in HiRISE) around a ~2 m pit
hirise: ESP_078339_2115 (2023-04-13, before) and ESP_087200_2115 (2025-03-03, after); same orbits as U19 and V19, not impact-targeted
evidence: Diffuse dark spot (~70 m; 74 x 130 m in CTX) on the plains among the Erebus Montes, in V19 2025-03-03 and V20 2025-04-17 (z -7.0, -8.5 on a 35 m disc; two orbits under the same sun); absent 2010-09-05 and 2023-04-13 (z +0.1, -0.2; r 0.71, 0.72), the 2023 image under the same sun (incidence 42.2 vs 42.1-42.6 deg), when a control 280 m WSW reads -4.7, -3.2. HiRISE took 0.5 m images on the U19 and V19 orbits (ESP_078339_2115, ESP_087200_2115; incidence 42.2, 42.6 deg; sub-solar azimuth 175, 176 deg), which align with correlation 0.94. Matched in brightness beyond 100 m, the 2025 image is 11% darker within 40 m of the spot (ratio 0.89 within 30 m, 0.96 at 30-60 m, 1.04 at 80-100 m; a 72 x 90 m zone below 0.93, minimum 0.75), and at its darkest point there is a new feature ~2 m across (four pixels), dark on its west side and bright on its east side under a western sun, as a small pit would be; it is absent in 2023, while a boulder 5 m NE is in both. HiRISE map position 31.0720 N 181.4846 E (the CTX and HiRISE map frames differ by ~600 m here). Window 2023-04 to 2025-03; the nearest catalogued impact is 60.1 km away (a 2012-2013 crater in Daubar et al. 2022); no MOC coverage.
alternatives: dust removed by a dust devil or wind (possible for the diffuse darkening, but it would not make a new pit at its centre); a boulder or its shadow (no: under a western sun a boulder is bright on its west side, like the one 5 m NE); an image artifact (no: the pit spans four pixels in a clean HiRISE image and sits at the centre of the darkening)

name: Tharsis lava plains 350 km W of Echus Chasma
size_m: ~33 (34x42), with a smaller dot ~70 m NW
evidence: Compact, very dark spot (~33 m; 34 x 42 m) with a smaller dark dot ~70 m NW, on smooth Tharsis lava plains 350 km W of Echus Chasma, in U16 2023-01-27, V20 2025-04-12 and V23 2025-07-05 (z -11.0, -13.5, -7.1 on a 17 m disc; r 0.34, 1, 0.33); absent in the only earlier image, B17 2010-01-23 (z +0.6, r 0.38), taken under a similar sun (incidence 44.2 vs 39.9 deg, azimuth 207 vs 192), in which a control 225 m SW reads -2.9 (-1.2 to -2.0 later). Window 2010-01 to 2023-01; the nearest catalogued impact is 91 km away; no MOC coverage; HiRISE ESP_087711_1820, taken with V20, falls 11 km away.
alternatives: dust devil or wind streak (unlikely: a round spot, no track, unchanged over 2.5 years); a compression artifact (excluded: the same spot on three orbits); a pre-existing feature lost in the 2010 image's noise (unlikely: the control feature, fainter in the later images, is clear in it)

name: western Arabia Terra, 5 km NNW of lead 57
size_m: ~55 (48x74) main spot in a dark cluster ~80x140
evidence: Irregular dark cluster ~80 x 140 m (a main spot ~55 m, 48 x 74 m, with smaller spots to its S) on eroded plains in western Arabia Terra, 5.2 km NNW of lead 57, in U20 2023-05-04, V17 2025-01-06, V18 2025-02-03 and V19 2025-03-25 (z -7.6, -8.0, -6.2, -4.5 on a 28 m disc); absent 2010-02-17 and 2014-03-18 (z -0.4, -0.5; r 0.28, 0.73), the 2014 image under the same sun as U20 (incidence 46.9 vs 45.4 deg, azimuth 204 vs 200); a weak control 300 m NE reads -1.0 and -0.8 in them. The same two images bracket lead 57, so both formed 2014-03 to 2023-05; CTX cannot tell whether they come from one body that broke up (5 km is far wider than typical impact clusters). Also detected as V19_087470_1990_r02 in V19's frame (~1.1 km offset). The nearest catalogued impact is 186 km away; no MOC coverage; HiRISE ESP_087470_1990, which shows lead 57, ends 4.0 km away.
alternatives: slope streaks or small dust avalanches (unlikely: no steep slope is visible at the spot, and the dark marks are blobs, not downslope streaks); dust devil (no track; persists two years); a pre-existing dark feature (excluded: the 2014 image under the same sun shows nothing)

name: CTX monitoring site in northern Amazonis Planitia
size_m: diffuse ~210 (172x292), two lobes in a N-S line
evidence: Diffuse dark zone ~210 m across (172 x 292 m in the before/after difference), two lobes in a N-S line, on flat ground between small knobs at a CTX monitoring site in northern Amazonis Planitia, in nine images from 2022-12-30 to 2026-01-30 (U15, U19, U23, V04, V09, V16, V20, W01, W06; z -6.9, -5.1, -3.9, -5.7, -7.9, -4.9, -5.3, -5.1, -2.5 on a 90 m disc; a control 260 m SSW reads -0.3 to -1.5 in the same images); absent 2010-08-31, 2021-10-27, 2022-03-03 and 2022-07-14 (z -0.7, -0.8, -0.7, -1.3; r 0.96, 0.88, 0.78, 0.69) and in six more aligned images back to 2009 in the verification. Same-sun comparisons: U01 2021-10 against U19 2023-04 (incidence 46.9 vs 43.9 deg) reads -0.8 then -5.1, and U10 2022-07 against V09 2024-05 (77.4 vs 78.3 deg, azimuth 136 vs 137) -1.3 then -7.9; a control 260 m SSW reads -0.8 to -1.7 in the earlier images. Window 2022-07 to 2022-12; the later images keep the site's monitoring rationale, none aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 25 km); the nearest catalogued impact is 55 km away (a cluster formed 2008-2012) and the 2021 S1094b crater 980 km; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: dust avalanches (slope streaks) on the knobs' flanks, perhaps set off together (possible, but much of the darkening, including the whole northern lobe, lies on flat ground between the knobs); dust removed by a dust devil or wind (no track; the patch stayed for three years); no crater is resolvable at 6-12 m per pixel, so the impact reading rests on the shape and the sudden onset

name: knobby floor of northern Orcus Patera
evidence: Compact dark core about 55 m across (48 x 114 m in V19; 56 x 56 m at half depth in the registered before/after difference) with fainter darkening around it, on knobby ground on the floor of northern Orcus Patera, in U16 2023-01-30, V19 2025-03-30 and W03 2025-10-04, three orbits (z -3.8, -7.0, -6.0 on a 50 m disc); absent 2010-08-18 and 2014-06-09 (z -1.0, -0.6; r 0.75, 0.40) under the same sun as the later images (incidence 49 and 51 deg, azimuth 197 and 193, against 40-54 deg and 180-204), and in a hazy 2009 image (r 0.18, not counted). The nearby control feature is faint (z -1.5 in 2010, -0.2 in 2014). Window 2014-06 to 2023-01; no image aimed at an impact (U16 and V19 target Orcus Patera, W03 is a HiRISE ride-along whose strip ends 34 km north); no HiRISE (nearest edge 10.8 km); the nearest catalogued new impact (Daubar 2022) is 156 km away and a CTX image of a dark spot first seen by MOC 120 km; no MOC coverage. It lies inside the InSight study area of Bickel et al. (2025), 44 deg from the lander, and its window overlaps that catalogue's period, but each of its 123 impacts has HiRISE images and this point has none.
alternatives: a dark slope streak on a knob's flank (Orcus Patera has many on its rim and ridges, but the knobs here are small and the core is compact rather than a downslope streak); dark material moved by wind, which makes dark spots and streaks elsewhere in Orcus Patera (no streak or track is visible); the 2023 image shows it less dark (z -3.8 under a higher sun), so it may have darkened later; no crater is resolvable at 5.6 m per pixel

name: lava plains of Echus Palus
evidence: Dark spot about 120-140 m across (134 x 162 m at half depth in V14 on the 2 m grid, contrast -7.3%; 148 x 196 m in V16) with a darker core about 60 m wide, on ridged lava plains of Echus Palus, in V14 2024-10-13 and V16 2024-12-30 (two orbits under the same sun, incidence 40 deg; z -8.5 and -6.5 on a 40 m disc); absent in P07 2007-05-20 (r 0.71, sun 19 deg lower; z +0.4), P15 2008-01-08 (similar sun, incidence 38; r 0.34; z +0.0) and N08 2020-07-18 (r 0.38, incidence 62; z -0.1), in which the nearby ridges are clear. The registered before/after difference is deepest in the 2 km crop at the spot (128 x 160 m at half depth). A control feature 195 m E reads z -2.0, -1.8 and -1.1 in the earlier images (weak), far fainter than the spot. V16's own map position is offset by about 520 m, which the registration corrects. Window 2020-07 to 2024-10; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 22.7 km); a catalogued candidate impact site lies 27 km away (HiRISE ESP_092563_1940 targeted it on 2026-04-25; the CTX note dates it between December 2010 and August 2025), far beyond the usual spread of a fragment cluster, so most likely a separate event; the nearest Daubar 2022 site is 130 km away; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: dust stripped by wind from a patch of the lava plain (but the spot is round, sits on no landform and has a sharp darker core); a deposit of dark sand (no source or bedforms nearby); no crater is resolvable at 5.5 m per pixel

name: lava plains N of Ascraeus Mons
evidence: Compact dark spot about 70 m across (88 x 76 m at half depth in N15 on the 2 m grid, contrast -6.6%; 88 x 74 m and -4.7% in V17, so fading) on knobby lava plains 250 km N of the summit of Ascraeus Mons, in N15 2021-02-12 and V17 2025-01-11 (two orbits; z -13.2 and -8.7 on a 35 m disc); in N15 a faint dark streak runs ~300 m NW from it and is gone by 2025, as a ray of a fresh blast zone would be. Absent in P16 2008-02-28 (r 0.65; z +0.1) under the same sun as V17 (incidence 40.5 and 40.6 deg, azimuth 192 and 188), in which the knobby texture around the site is clear. The registered before/after difference at the spot (72 x 60 m at half depth, z -7.3) is matched in the 2 km crop only by contrast differences inside a 100 m crater 1 km NE. A control feature 250 m W reads z -3.2 in P16 (positive). Window 2008-02 to 2021-02; only one earlier image; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 28.9 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 51 km away (a candidate site imaged by CTX and HiRISE in 2023, formed between January 2021 and November 2022), the nearest Daubar 2022 site 158 km; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: a dust devil that stalled (the 2021 streak could be its track), but dust devil marks usually fade within a few years and this spot was still clear four years later; dust stripped by wind from a patch; the earlier image is high in contrast and shows knob shadows near the site, but none like the spot under the same sun; no crater is resolvable at 5.5 m per pixel

name: Arabia Terra, 97 km W of Flammarion crater
evidence: Compact, very dark spot about 55 to 60 m across (58 x 58 m at half depth in V16 on the 2 m grid, contrast -8%; 56 x 54 m and -11% in W03) on smooth plains of Arabia Terra 97 km W of Flammarion crater, in V16 2024-12-06 and W03 2025-10-17 (two orbits; z -9.9 and -13.6 on a 25 m disc). Absent in G04 2010-10-03 (r 0.50; z -1.0) under the same sun as W03 (incidence 52.3 and 53.1 deg, azimuth 180 and 182) and in U09 2022-06-21 (r 0.36; z -1.4; incidence 69 deg). A small fresh crater 300 m E and the pits around the site are in all four images. The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (72 x 64 m at half depth, z -4.6) and nowhere else in the 2 km crop. A control feature reads z -3.2 in G04 and -2.6 in U09 (positive). Window 2022-06 to 2024-12; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 18.6 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 103 km away (a CTX candidate site formed between 2007 and 2018), the nearest Daubar 2022 site 217 km; no MOC coverage; lead 8 is 74 km away.
alternatives: a dust devil that stalled, but no dust-devil tracks are visible in the 2 km crops and the spot was still as dark ten months later; dust stripped by wind from a patch, which seldom leaves so round and sharp a spot; the 2022 image has a low sun (69 deg) and moderate alignment, so the window could start as early as 2010; no crater is resolvable at 5.6 m per pixel

name: Arabia Terra, 116 km N of Barth crater
evidence: Compact dark spot about 25 m across (22 x 28 m at half depth in V15 on the 2 m grid, contrast -4%; 20 x 28 m and -5% in V17) on smooth ground in Arabia Terra 116 km N of Barth crater, in V15 2024-11-14 and V17 2025-01-03 (two orbits; z -10.8 and -8.9 on a 20 m disc). Absent in five earlier images: B17 2010-01-28 (r 0.41; z +0.4) under nearly the same sun as V17 (incidence 42.9 and 40.7 deg), three images from 2012 (r 0.26 to 0.30; z -0.5 to +0.6) and U16 2023-01-11 (r 0.40), taken under the same sun as V15 (incidence 38.7 and 38.0 deg). U16 has no automatic score; measured on the registered crops it reads +0.2 at the spot (mean z on the disc) against -2.0 and -2.6 in V15 and V17. A pre-existing dark blob 100 m S is in every image. The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (40 x 44 m at half depth, z -2.4). Window 2023-01 to 2024-11; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 17.9 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 101 km away (a HiRISE candidate site imaged in 2023), the nearest Daubar 2022 site 141 km; no MOC coverage; no comparable dark feature lies within 300 m, so the control is not informative.
alternatives: dark material moved by wind into a small round patch on smooth ground, which would be unusual and would have to persist unchanged for seven weeks; a dust devil that stalled; at 25 m the spot is only four or five pixels across, so its shape is poorly resolved; the earlier images are only moderately aligned (r 0.26 to 0.41)

name: northern Cyane Fossae, 250 km NE of lead 21
evidence: Compact dark spot about 80 m across (94 x 82 m at half depth on the 2 m grid in V14 2024-10-28, 104 x 92 m in U15) on knobby plains in northern Cyane Fossae, 4 km W of a pit chain, in four images on four orbits: U15 2022-12-25, V12 2024-08-12, V14 2024-10-11 and V14 2024-10-28 (z -8.7, -4.8, -6.0 and -5.6 on a 40 m disc). Absent in three well-aligned earlier images: P14 2007-12-20 under the same sun as U15 (incidence 43.9 and 46.2 deg, azimuth 153 and 151; r 0.89, z 0.0), G18 2011-12-30 (r 0.72; z -0.6) and N09 2020-08-23 (incidence 71 deg; r 0.94; z -0.2). The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (124 x 96 m at half depth, z -3.0) and nowhere else in the 2 km crop. A control feature 250 m ENE reads z -2.2 in P14 and -2.0 in N09 (positive). Window 2020-08 to 2022-12; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 22 km; the HiRISE image taken together with V12 misses the spot); the nearest catalogued new impact is 89 km away (a cluster that formed between 2014-03 and 2017-11; Daubar 2022); no MOC coverage; lead 21 is 253 km away.
alternatives: a faint thin dark line runs SW from the spot in V12 and both V14 images and may show faintly in N09, so a dust devil that stalled at the end of its track is possible, though the spot is far darker and wider than the line; dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: compact, and it appeared between two images 2.3 years apart)

name: Medusae Fossae Formation, 295 km W of Gordii Dorsum
size_m: ~60 (66x76), ragged ray-like margins; HiRISE: 76x81 dark zone with a ~2 m pit
hirise: ESP_086777_1840 (2025-01-30, same orbit as V17, terrain sample, not impact-targeted)
evidence: Compact dark spot about 60 m across (66 x 76 m at half depth on the 2 m grid) with ragged, ray-like margins on wind-ridged ground of the Medusae Fossae Formation, 295 km W of Gordii Dorsum, in V16 2024-12-21, V17 2025-01-30 and V23 2025-07-25 (three orbits; z -13.4, -12.6 and -11.1 on a 30 m disc). Absent in B09 2009-05-18 (r 0.44; z -0.5; incidence 51.1 deg) and N04 2020-03-12 (r 0.31; z -0.5), the latter under nearly the same sun as V23 (incidence 53.4 and 55.4 deg) but 31 deg off nadir. alternatives: dark ground laid bare by the wind (the main alternative: the patch is irregular with only a faint core, it lies at the edge of a knob field where the wind can strip dust, and new dark wind bands formed 2 km away in 2023-2024; against it, the patch is roughly round rather than streaked, it was already there in 2023-03, before those bands formed, and it fades as a blast zone does); a dust devil (no tracks, and it lasts at least 22 months); shading (P16 has the same sun as V16 and shows nothing, and the patch shows under sun directions 50 deg apart); an image defect (four orbits); only one usable earlier image, a window fifteen years long, and U18 and V16 poorly aligned (r 0.15 and 0.23); a real change, but a shape the wind could make, so PROMISING

name: northern Arabia Terra, south of Deuteronilus Mensae
evidence: Irregular dark spot with a darker core on cratered plains of northern Arabia Terra, z -6.5 on 2025-08-02; absent 2010-01, 2021-05 and 2021-08 under similar sun (42-47 deg vs 46 deg; z +0.4 to +1.1, r 0.24-0.28) while a dark feature 207 m away reads z -2.3 to -3.4. One image.

name: plains east of Arsia Mons

impact_targeted_images: W01_089298_1973 is itself targeted at an older (2014-2018) impact 16.2 km away

name: central Arabia Terra, east of Tikhonravov crater (cluster)

name: floor of Denning crater
evidence: Very dark compact blob 80-100 m across on the floor of Denning crater, beside a small pre-existing crater, on 2025-09-10 (z -4.3, 30 m disc); absent 2012-06-19, 2020-07-29 and 2025-06-14 (r 0.72, 0.40, 0.68; 2025-06 under nearly the same sun, incidence 66 vs 65 deg), while a feature 295 m away reads z -1.4 to -2.5. name: Medusae Fossae Formation near Eumenides Dorsum
evidence: Diffuse dark patch 150-200 m across with a faint darker centre on yardang-textured Medusae Fossae Formation near Eumenides Dorsum, in 4 images from 4 orbits 2023-09-02 to 2025-10-09 (z -3.6 to -5.8 on a 70 m disc; sun azimuth 197 to 216 deg); absent 2008-06-14 (r 0.70) under the same sun (incidence 52 vs 55 deg) and 2011-12-28 (r 0.34). The control is uninformative: the darkest feature near the spot in 2008, 253 m SE, reads only z -1.4. Window 2011-12 to 2023-09; the nearest catalogued impact is 40.4 km away.
alternatives: wind-driven albedo change on dusty yardang terrain (nearly as good: diffuse, low contrast, no resolved core); dust devil (less likely: no track in four images)

name: Amazonis Planitia (rayed spot with satellite dots)
evidence: Dark spot 100-130 m across with short rays and a scatter of small satellite dark dots on Amazonis Planitia, in one image, V18 2025-02-08 (z -6.5 on a 55 m disc); absent in four earlier images, 2008-06-30, 2014-05-11, 2022-06-30 and 2023-01-24 (r 0.27-0.56; the 2008 and 2014 images under a similar sun, incidence 47 and 51 vs 42 deg). The control is uninformative: the darkest nearby feature reads only z -0.3 to -0.9 before. Window 2023-01 to 2025-02; the nearest catalogued impact is 53 km away. One image.
alternatives: image artifact (unlikely: the rays and dots are arranged around the spot); dust devil (unlikely: rayed pattern, no track)

name: plains N of Pavonis Mons (spot with a tail)
evidence: Dark spot (core ~85x130 m) with a broad dark tail ~600 m long to the ESE on the plains N of Pavonis Mons, in one image, V17 2025-01-25 (z -6.1 on a 45 m disc); absent 2010-03-08 and 2014-04-22 (r 0.56, 0.77; incidence 46 and 51 vs 43 deg), when a control 300 m ESE reads z -1.7 and -1.1 and the spot -0.1 and -0.0. Window 2014-04 to 2025-01; the nearest HiRISE image targets a different small fresh crater 10 km away (2012). One image.
alternatives: dust devil or wind streak (nearly as good for the tail, less so for the compact head); an impact whose dark blast deposit was blown downwind

name: Daedalia Planum, 8 km SE of Lead 42
evidence: Irregular dark spot ~60x70 m on Daedalia Planum, 8 km SE of Lead 42, in one image, V22 2025-06-30 (z -7.0 on a 25 m disc); absent 2007-12-21 and 2008-08-12 (r 0.86, 0.95, the second under the same sun; the spot reads +0.1 and +0.8 while a control 145 m SE reads -1.5 and -2.6) and not seen in K11 2018-11-30 (noisy, high sun, but it shows Lead 42). Window 2018-11 to 2025-06 (2008-08 to 2025-06 if K11 is set aside); the nearest catalogued impact is 84.7 km away. One image.
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (possible: irregular outline); image artifact (unlikely: smooth blob, no line pattern)

name: northern Arabia Terra
evidence: Irregular dark patch ~70 m across at the edge of a brighter ridge in northern Arabia Terra, in V18 2025-02-15 and V20 2025-04-17 (z -4.6, -4.7 on a 22 m disc); absent 2008-10-21 (r 0.90, incidence 51 vs 42 deg), when the spot reads +0.3 and a control 300 m N -4.6. Window 2008-10 to 2025-02; the nearest catalogued impact is 89.8 km away.
alternatives: new slope streak (nearly as good: rugged terrain, irregular patch beside a slope); shading under a higher sun (unlikely: the 2025 sun is higher, which weakens shadows)

name: terrain NE of Fesenkov crater
evidence: Cluster of dark spots (main core ~45x35 m, smaller dots to the W and NE) NE of Fesenkov crater, in V20 2025-04-08 (z -3.6 on a 20 m disc) and faintly at the same place in U10 2022-07-10 (z -2.6); absent 2008-05-10 under the same sun as V20 (incidence 42 vs 44 deg, r 0.68; the spot reads +0.3 while a control 275 m NNE reads -6.3) and 2020-07-29 (r 0.26). Window 2020-07 to 2022-07 (2008-05 to 2022-07 if the poorly aligned 2020 image is set aside); the nearest catalogued impact is 66.5 km away.
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (possible: low contrast in 2022); a cluster impact is the most natural reading of the satellite dots

name: central Arabia Terra
evidence: Compact dark spot (core ~50x60 m) in central Arabia Terra, in one image, V17 2025-01-20 (z -7.3 on a 20 m disc); absent 2007-12-21 under the same sun (incidence 39 vs 40 deg, r 0.64), when the spot reads -1.3 and a control 275 m NNE -8.1. Window 2007-12 to 2025-01; the nearest catalogued impact is 39 km away. One image.
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (possible over 17 years, less likely for a round spot); image artifact (unlikely: smooth round blob)

name: plains N of Avernus Colles (InSight study area)
evidence: Compact dark spot (core ~50x40 m) on the plains N of Avernus Colles, in one image, V17 2025-01-21 (z -14.9 on a 20 m disc); absent 2010-10-11 (r 0.81, incidence 54 vs 44 deg), when the spot reads +1.8 and a control 170 m W -2.7. The nearest catalogued impact is 79.1 km away. One image.
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: compact and very dark); image artifact (unlikely: smooth round blob)

name: Fortuna Fossae region (N of Noctis Labyrinthus)
evidence: Compact dark spot (core ~45x35 m) in the Fortuna Fossae region N of Noctis Labyrinthus, in one image, V18 2025-02-10 (z -11.2 on a 20 m disc); absent 2008-10-15 and 2008-12-26 (r 0.71, 0.47; incidence 54 and 57 vs 45 deg), when the spot reads -0.2 and -0.1 and a control 245 m N -4.3 and -2.8. alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (unlikely: compact and very dark); image artifact (unlikely: smooth round blob)

Window 2014-01 to 2025-03; the nearest catalogued impact is 46 km away. One image.
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (possible over 11 years, less likely for a compact spot); image artifact (unlikely: smooth blob)

name: eastern Tharsis lava flows NE of Tharsis Tholus

Window 2016-07 to 2025-02; the nearest catalogued impact is 73 km away. One image.
alternatives: dark substrate exposed by wind (nearly as good: diffuse); cloud shadow (unlikely at this size and sharpness, but only a second image can exclude it)

name: floor of Henry crater, Arabia Terra

name: Ulysses Fossae (between Olympus and Ascraeus Mons)
evidence: Diffuse dark patch with 2-3 darker blobs on very dusty Tharsis lava plains; absent twice under the same sun (57 deg); no landform at the spot.
alternatives: one-image artifact (cannot fully reject); wind or dust-devil darkening (possible, diffuse)

name: western Noctis Labyrinthus, plains between the troughs
evidence: Compact, very dark spot (core ~45 m) with a faint dark smudge ~60 m to its NW, on the smooth plains between the troughs of western Noctis Labyrinthus, in one image, V22 2025-06-03 (z -17.6 on an 18 m disc); absent 2008-07-11 under the same sun (incidence 58 vs 59 deg, azimuth 222 vs 221; r 0.76) and 2016-04-11 (r 0.84), when the spot reads -0.0 and -0.1, with the knobs and a 500 m crater ~800 m SW lined up. alternatives: image artifact (unlikely: a smooth spot with a halo, not a pixel defect); dust devil caught in the act (unlikely: dark, with no bright column or track); only a second image can exclude a transient

name: Arabia Terra, 26 km NW of the rim of Janssen crater
evidence: Compact dark spot (~60 m) at the edge of a brighter, rougher unit in Arabia Terra, 26 km NW of the rim of Janssen crater, in one image, V21 2025-05-29 (z -4.3 on an 18 m disc); absent 2008-03-05 and 2018-03-11 (z +0.6, +0.2; r 0.63, 0.62), the 2018 image under a similar sun (incidence 51 vs 53 deg, azimuth 205 vs 217), while a control 225 m N reads -3.0 and -2.0.
