alternatives: slope streak off the edge of the bright unit (possible: it sits at a low scarp, though it is round, not a tapering streak); dust devil or wind-exposed patch (possible over 7 years); one-image artifact

name: knobby Tharsis plains 315 km S of Pavonis Mons
evidence: Compact dark spot (core ~40-50 m) with faint dark streaks radiating from it and a diffuse dark zone, among the knobs of the Tharsis plains 315 km S of Pavonis Mons, in V18_086868 2025-02-06 and V18_086934 2025-02-11 (z -9.6, -11.4 on a 20 m disc; two orbits under the same sun). The 2023-02-06 image (U17; oblique at 27 deg emission, 6.6 m pixels, heavily compressed; r 0.49) shows only a faint ~25 m dark blob at the same place (z -3.0), and 2009-03-26 (r 0.32, sun from a different azimuth) a faint mark (z -1.2); a knob 300 m E reads -2.9, -6.4, -10.1, -7.2 in the four images. The CTX map positions of these images differ by up to 3.4 km; each was re-centred with wide_register.py before the usual registration. Window 2009-03 (or 2023-02) to 2025-02; the nearest catalogued impact is 72.8 km away; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: a small pre-existing dark feature darkened and enlarged by wind (possible: something faint was there in 2023); the spot formed before 2023 and the poor 2023 image under-shows it (possible); a fresh impact after 2023 fits the rays best

name: lava plains at the SE margin of Ceraunius Fossae, 525 km N of Ascraeus Mons
evidence: Compact dark spot (~34 m; 44 x 32 m) beside a small knob on cratered lava plains at the SE margin of Ceraunius Fossae, 525 km N of Ascraeus Mons, in one image, V20 2025-04-20 (z -9.8 on a 15 m disc); absent 2023-07-13 under the same sun (incidence 47 vs 45 deg, azimuth 203 vs 201; r 0.80), when the spot reads -0.7 and a shadowed crater 300 m ENE -6.9 (-7.9 in V20), and in 2013-07-22 and 2013-12-01 (r 0.52, 0.72); a third 2013 image (D19_034805) ends at the spot and is not counted. The spot lies on the knob's sunward side, so it is not the knob's shadow. Window 2023-07 to 2025-04 (21 months); the nearest catalogued impact is 70.1 km away (a 2005-2016 CTX candidate, a different site); no MOC coverage. One image.
alternatives: dust devil caught in the act or a fresh dust-devil scour (possible, though there is no track); dark material exposed on the knob's flank by wind (possible); one-image artifact (unlikely: a smooth blob, not a pixel defect); only a second image can exclude a transient

name: knob chain in the Fortuna Fossae region, 400 km SSW of Tharsis Tholus
evidence: Very dark spot (~42 m; 46 x 62 m) with a faint halo on the sunward (SW) side of a small knob at the end of a knob chain, on lava plains in the Fortuna Fossae region 400 km SSW of Tharsis Tholus, in one image, V17 2025-01-29 (z -7.7 on an 18 m disc); absent 2012-01-09 under an identical sun (incidence 43.5 vs 43.5 deg, azimuth 208 vs 202; r 0.53) and 2008-05-29 (r 0.74), when the spot reads -0.1 and -1.3, with the knob itself visible in both. The control (a knob shadow 210 m ENE) is weak: -2.1, -1.2, -3.0. Window 2012-01 to 2025-01; the nearest catalogued impact is 102.1 km away; lead 49 is ~100 km SE; no MOC coverage. One image.
alternatives: the knob's shadow (excluded: the spot is on the sunward side and absent under the identical 2012 sun); dark material shed off the knob (possible); dust devil (no track); one-image artifact (unlikely)

name: Tharsis plains 490 km S of Ascraeus Mons
evidence: Compact, very dark spot (~19 m; 16 x 22 m) on the Tharsis lava plains 490 km S of Ascraeus Mons, in one heavily compressed image, V19 2025-03-29 (z -10.5 on a 12 m disc); absent 2012-02-20 under the same sun (incidence 49.7 vs 51.2 deg, azimuth 217 vs 215), 2012-09-15, 2022-06-19 and 2024-04-08 (z +1.5, -0.1, +0.1, +1.0; r 0.60, 0.69, 0.54, 0.34), when a control 280 m E reads -4.1, -3.6, -3.4 and, in the poorly aligned 2024 image, -1.0. Window 2024-04 to 2025-03 (2022-06 to 2025-03 if the 2024 image is set aside); the nearest catalogued impact is 14.3 km away (a CTX candidate formed 2007-12 to 2008-02, a different site); no MOC coverage. One image.
alternatives: a compression artifact (possible: the image is heavily compressed, though the spot is a smooth blob about four pixels across, not a block); dust devil caught in the act (possible; no track); only a second image can exclude a transient

name: plains west of Echus Chasma, 16 km north of lead 63
evidence: Compact dark spot about 45 m across (48 x 50 m at half depth in V18, 46 m in U18) with a lobe to the NW, on wind-textured plains west of Echus Chasma, 16.5 km N of lead 63 and found in the same image pair, in U18 2023-03-29 and V18 2025-02-12 (two orbits under the same sun: incidence 47 and 46 deg, azimuth 206); absent 2006-12-22 and 2012-10-12 (z +1.0, +0.5 on a 25 m disc; r 0.53, 0.42) under suns 6-9 deg lower, which would lengthen any shadow. It is faint: z -3.5 in V18 and only -1.2 in the hazy U18 image on the 25 m disc, although with the km-scale brightness gradient removed it is the darkest point within 200 m in both later images (z -4.6, -4.4 on a 20 m disc) and reads +0.4 and -0.2 in the earlier ones; the registered before/after difference has its deepest change in the 2 km crop at the spot (52 x 72 m at half depth). A control feature 300 m NE reads z -2.7 and -1.6 in the earlier images (weak to moderate). Window 2012-10 to 2023-03; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 12.5 km, a 2026 image of the chasma rim); the nearest catalogued new impact is 62 km away (a 2.8 m crater in Echus Chasma, Daubar 2022); no MOC coverage.
alternatives: dust stripped by wind from a small patch, for example in the lee of a knob (the plains are wind-textured, and a faint change like this is what such stripping can look like); the hazy 2023 image shows only a smudge, so the case rests mostly on the blocky, compressed 2025 image; a fragment of the event that made lead 63 (same window) is unlikely 16.5 km away; no crater is resolvable at 5.4 m per pixel

name: western Terra Sabaea, 210 km S of Tuscaloosa crater
evidence: Compact round dark spot about 55 m across (58 x 52 m at half depth on the 2 m grid, contrast -5.7%) with a darker core about 20 m wide, on flat ground 100 m SW of a dark knobby ridge in western Terra Sabaea, in V21 2025-05-27 (incidence 57 deg, z -4.1 on a 30 m disc); absent in G01 2010-07-08 under the same sun (incidence 56, azimuth 217 vs 220; r 0.79; z -0.3) and in the striped J04 2016-06-27 (incidence 51; r 0.50; z -0.2). The registered before/after difference has its deepest change in the 2 km crop at the spot (72 x 72 m at half depth). A control feature 260 m NE (a dark knob on the ridge) reads z -3.0 in G01 and -1.4 in J04, as in V21 (-3.1): positive in 2010. Only one image shows the spot. Window 2016-06 to 2025-05; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 24.7 km, a 2025 dune survey on the same orbit as V21); the nearest catalogued new impact is 88 km away (a candidate site imaged by CTX in 2016; the 3 m cluster of Daubar 2022 is 97 km away); no MOC coverage.
alternatives: dust stripped by wind from a small patch at the foot of the ridge (bedforms lie just east of it); a dark boulder or outcrop exposed by dust removal; with a single image, a short-lived surface change cannot be excluded, although the spot is round with a sharp darker core; no crater is resolvable at 5.3 m per pixel

name: plains W of Ascraeus Mons
evidence: Compact, very dark spot about 60 m across (60 x 64 m at half depth on the 2 m grid, contrast -8%) inside a diffuse dark halo, on knobby lava plains W of Ascraeus Mons, 25 km W of Ascraeus Mensa, in V16 2024-12-02 only (z -7.0 on a 30 m disc). Absent in seven earlier images from 2008 to 2022 (z -0.2 to +0.7), among them D17 2013-10-12 under nearly the same sun as V16 (incidence 40.4 and 38.6 deg, azimuth 195 and 180), two F14 images from 2015 (incidence 38 and 40 deg) and U06 2022-03-16 (incidence 59 deg). The ground at the site is almost featureless at CTX scale, so the earlier images align poorly (r 0.30 or less) and two of them (P20 2008-06-07 and B22 2010) show no texture at all. The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (68 x 76 m at half depth, z -5.5) and nowhere else in the 2 km crop. Window 2022-03 to 2024-12; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 6.3 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 54 km away (a crater 3.6 m across that formed between 2008-06 and 2014-08; Daubar 2022); no MOC coverage; the control feature is not detected in any earlier image (z -0.8 or above), so the control is not informative; lead 29 is 325 km away.
alternatives: one image only, so an image defect cannot be fully excluded, though the halo grades into the ground; a dust devil that stalled, though no tracks show in the 2 km crop; because the earlier images are low in contrast and the control is not detected in them, a faint pre-existing dark patch cannot be ruled out, though nothing as dark as this spot shows in any of the seven

name: south-eastern Ulysses Fossae
evidence: Compact dark spot about 40 m across (34 x 44 m at half depth on the 2 m grid, contrast -7%) on flat lava plains about 150 m W of the foot of a NE-SW ridge in south-eastern Ulysses Fossae, in V16 2024-12-21 only (z -8.8 on a 25 m disc). Absent in three well-aligned earlier images: B19 2010-03-12 (r 0.80; z +0.3; incidence 45.9 vs 40.4 deg), U10 2022-07-19 (r 0.58; z 0.0) and V09 2024-05-13 (r 0.68; z -0.3), taken 222 days before V16. Knobs and small dark marks around the site are in every image. The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (48 x 56 m at half depth, z -2.7). A control feature reads z -7.0 in B19 and -2.2 in U10 (positive). Three further CTX images listed for the site cannot be used: F08 2014-11-30 has no data there, and F16 2015-07-09 and J10 2016-12-20 are offset by more than the 3 km registration window. Window 2024-05 to 2024-12; no HiRISE (nearest edge 14.4 km; the HiRISE image taken together with V16 misses the spot); F16 was aimed at a catalogued new crater 15.8 m across 20 km away that formed between 2011-10 and 2014-11 (Daubar 2022), a separate and older event; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: one image only, so an image defect cannot be fully excluded, though the spot has a diffuse margin and sits on the ground texture; a dust devil that stalled; dark material shed from the ridge 150 m away, though no streak links the two

name: Lucus Planum (Medusae Fossae Formation)
size_m: ~80-100 diffuse (84x64 in the registered difference), no distinct core
evidence: Diffuse dark patch about 80 to 100 m across (84 x 64 m at half depth in the registered before/after difference, z -1.9) that darkens both the ground and the shaded troughs of the wind-eroded ridges on Lucus Planum (Medusae Fossae Formation), 139 km E of Tartarus Scopulus. It is faint in V16 2024-12-09 and clear in V18 2025-02-19 and V21 2025-05-13 (three orbits; z -4.0, -5.0 and -5.9 on a 35 m disc). Absent in B19 2010-03-16 (r 0.68; z -1.2, from the trough shadows) under the same sun as V18 (incidence 53.0 and 51.1 deg, azimuth 220 and 214); the ridge texture of B19 lines up with the later images. The difference is deepest at the patch and nowhere else in the 2 km crop. A control feature reads z -3.3 in B19 (positive). Window 2010-03 to 2024-12 (one earlier image); no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 8.6 km; the HiRISE image taken together with V21 misses the patch); the nearest catalogued new impact is 81 km away (a candidate site imaged in 2021, formed between 2009 and 2020), the nearest Daubar 2022 site 289 km; no MOC coverage. It lies 44.8 deg from InSight, inside the area and period of Bickel et al. (2025), but every entry there has a HiRISE image and this site has none.
alternatives: a wind-driven albedo change (dust removed from a patch of the yardang surface), which the diffuse outline and the lack of a distinct core allow about as well as an impact; the floor-wide darkenings rejected elsewhere on the Medusae Fossae Formation had no centre, whereas this change is local and centred; the single earlier image leaves a 15-year window

name: 273 km NW of Reuyl crater
size_m: ~110 diffuse with a darker core (106x170; 112x220 in the registered difference)
evidence: Diffuse dark patch about 110 m across with a darker core (106 x 170 m at half depth on the 2 m grid in V17; 112 x 220 m in the registered before/after difference, elongated N-S) on mantled plains 273 km NW of Reuyl crater, in V17 2025-01-03 and V21 2025-05-04 (two orbits; z -4.9 and -2.7 on a 55 m disc). Absent in four earlier images from 2014 to 2022, where the site reads slightly bright (z +0.6 to +0.9): F03 2014-06-27, F06 2014-09-17, N06 2020-05-01 under the same sun as V21 (incidence 58.0 and 57.0 deg; r 0.68) and U10 2022-07-20 (r 0.42). The difference is deepest at the patch (z -4.0) and nowhere else in the 2 km crop. A control feature 195 m N reads z -2.3 in F06, -2.7 in N06 and -2.9 in U10 (positive). Position recentred 60 m SSE of the detection, on the darkest point of V17. Window 2022-07 to 2025-01; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 47 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 51 km away (a candidate site imaged in 2024 that formed between 2020-05 and 2022-12), a separate event; no MOC coverage. It lies 30.2 deg from InSight, inside the area of Bickel et al. (2025), but it formed after 2022-07 and has no HiRISE image, so it is very probably not in that catalogue.
alternatives: a diffuse albedo change (dust removed from a patch of the mantle by wind or a dust devil), which the soft outline, the N-S elongation and the weaker darkening in V21 allow about as well as an impact; the site was slightly bright before, so the removal of a bright dust patch would also darken it

name: Arabia Terra, 165 km NE of Schoner crater
size_m: ~150-200 rayed blast zone (188x222) with a bright central dot
evidence: Dark rayed blast zone about 150 to 200 m across (188 x 222 m at half depth on the 2 m grid; 240 x 316 m in the registered before/after difference) with a small bright dot near its centre, on smooth plains in Arabia Terra 165 km NE of Schoner crater, in V16 2024-12-07 only (z -7.4 on a 60 m disc). Absent in five earlier images: G14 2011-08-26 under the same sun (incidence 40.1 and 41.2 deg; r 0.33; z -0.5), D03 2012-08-01 (r 0.41; z -1.9), D06 2012-11-19 and 2012-11-30 (r 0.31, 0.32) and N10 2020-09-04 (incidence 65 deg; r 0.25). K10 2018-10-07 could not be registered and is not used. The difference is deepest at the spot (z -3.2) and nowhere else in the 2 km crop. The control feature is not detected in any earlier image (z -0.4 or above), so the control is not informative. Position recentred 53 m ESE of the detection. Window 2020-09 to 2024-12; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 35 km); the nearest catalogued new impacts are 55.6 km (a dark spot imaged by HiRISE in 2007) and 57.8 km away (a crater 15.6 m across that formed between 2001 and 2005; Daubar 2022), both separate and older; no MOC coverage; lead 79 is 343 km away.
alternatives: one image only, so an image defect cannot be fully excluded, though the rays and the bright centre are hard to make that way and the striping of V16 is uniform across the crop; a dust devil that stalled (unlikely: radial rays, no tracks)

name: plains N of western Tithonium Chasma, 72 km S of lead 47
evidence: Compact black spot about 35 m across (36 x 46 m at half depth on the 2 m grid) on rippled plains N of western Tithonium Chasma, 72 km S of lead 47, in V16 2024-12-05 only (z -13.0 on an 18 m disc). Absent in three earlier images: P12 2007-10-31 (r 0.67; z -1.9 from ripple shading; incidence 33.0 vs 40.6 deg), B01 2008-09-17 (r 0.61; z -0.9) and N03 2020-02-13 (r 0.49; z -1.4). Two more images cannot be used: P10 2007-08-20 is hazy from the 2007 global dust storm (r 0.17), and V20 2025-04-16 has the spot in the dark strip along its edge. The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (44 x 48 m at half depth, z -2.1). A control feature reads z -1.6 in P12, where the spot reads -1.9, so the control is between. Window 2020-02 to 2024-12; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 20.7 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 72 km away (a candidate site imaged by HiRISE in 2026), a separate event; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: one image only, so an image defect cannot be fully excluded, though the spot sits on the ripple texture and has a faint halo; a dust devil that stalled (no tracks in the 2 km crop); the earlier images were taken under other suns (incidence 33 to 57 deg against 41), but none shows anything as dark

name: plains among the Aeolis Mensae, 325 km N of Gale crater
evidence: Compact black spot about 30 m across (24 x 34 m at half depth on the 2 m grid) with a faint halo on plains among the Aeolis Mensae, 1 km NW of a mesa and 160 m N of a small pre-existing crater, 325 km N of Gale crater, in V15 2024-11-20 only (z -19.1 on a 15 m disc). Absent in six earlier images from 2009 to 2022 (z -0.7 to +1.1), among them B11 2009-07-20 under the same sun (incidence 39.0 and 38.0 deg; r 0.31; z +0.1) and U11 2022-08-12 (r 0.37; z +1.1). The plains are smooth at CTX scale, so the earlier images align only moderately (r 0.22 to 0.37); the small crater 160 m S lines up in all of them. D13 2013-06-12 could not be registered and is not used. The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (48 x 52 m at half depth, z -1.7) and nowhere else in the 2 km crop. A control feature (the small crater) reads z -7.1 in B11 and -8.4 in U11 (positive). Window 2022-08 to 2024-11; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 28.4 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 44 km away (a small fresh crater imaged by HiRISE in 2024-11), a separate event; no MOC coverage. It lies 5.3 deg from InSight, inside the area of Bickel et al. (2025), but it formed after 2022-08 and has no HiRISE image, so it is very probably not in that catalogue.
alternatives: one image only, so an image defect cannot be fully excluded: V15 carries a thin vertical line defect 300 m E of the spot, though the spot is round with a graded halo rather than a line or a block; a dust devil that stalled (no tracks in the 2 km crop)

name: Elysium Planitia (twin dark spot)
evidence: Pair of compact dark spots on smooth Elysium plains, identical in 3 images 2024-08 to 2025-12 at 40-58 deg incidence; absent in all 3 images from 2006-2008 (z +0.75, +0.04, +0.07) at 40-53 deg while a pre-existing dark spot 190 m away is detected in each (z -4.0, -2.4, -2.2), so the non-detections are real. No CTX image of the site exists between 2008-01 and 2024-08.
alternatives: dark material exposed by wind (unlikely: two compact spots, stable for 16 months); registration error (excluded: the neighbouring spot lines up in every epoch). PROMISING, not STRONG, only because no earlier image reaches the rule's alignment r >= 0.3 (best 0.22, featureless plains)

name: northern Acheron Fossae, 275 km N of lead 13
size_m: ~50 (82x48), a darker core ~20 m in a diffuse halo
evidence: Compact dark spot about 50 m across (82 x 48 m at half depth on the 2 m grid) with a darker core about 20 m wide and a diffuse halo, at the S edge of hummocky terrain in northern Acheron Fossae, 275 km N of lead 13, in V14 2024-10-21 only (z -6.4 on a 25 m disc). Absent in four earlier images from 2010 to 2018 (z -0.0 to +0.6), all aligned: B21 2010-05-11 (r 0.67), G20 2012-02-26 (r 0.77), J05 2016-07-16 (r 0.73) and K04 2018-04-08 under nearly the same sun (incidence 52.6 and 54.6 deg; r 0.40). The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (64 x 60 m at half depth, z -2.9) and nowhere else in the 2 km crop. A control feature 276 m E reads z -1.3 to -3.0 in the earlier images and -2.3 in V14, so a feature of that contrast shows in all of them. Window 2018-04 to 2024-10; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 65.7 km; the HiRISE images taken with B21, J05 and V14 lie 123, 159 and 109 km away); the nearest catalogued new impact is 201 km away; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: one image only, so an image defect cannot be fully excluded: V14 carries a thin vertical line defect about 220 m E of the spot, though the spot is round with a graded halo; a dust devil that stalled (no tracks in the 2 km crop); a wind-driven albedo change at the edge of the hummocky terrain

name: northern Amazonis Planitia, 427 km SW of lead 73
evidence: Compact dark spot about 50 m across (62 x 66 m at half depth on the 2 m grid) on knobby plains in northern Amazonis Planitia, 427 km SW of lead 73, in V16 2024-12-27 only (z -8.5 on a 25 m disc). A small pre-existing knob or pit sits at its NW edge: it shows as a small dark mark in P15, a shadowed knob in G05 and the NW lobe of the dark feature in V16. The spot is absent in P15 2008-01-21 under the same sun (incidence 43.6 and 43.9 deg, azimuth 158 and 159 deg; r 0.38, z -0.8), so it is not a shadow, and in G05 2010-11-15 under a low sun (incidence 60 deg; z +0.7), which aligns poorly (r 0.11) although the knobs around the site line up. In the registered difference against P15 the spot is the only compact dark change in the 2 km crop (64 x 52 m at half depth, z -2.3); a broad brightness gradient along the crop's W edge is deeper. A control feature reads z -1.8 in P15 (between). Window 2010-11 to 2024-12; no image aimed at an impact; P15 was taken to monitor dust raising in northern Amazonis; no HiRISE (nearest edge 25.5 km; the HiRISE image taken with V16 lies 120 km away); the nearest catalogued new impact is 120 km away (a CTX candidate site formed 2017-12 to 2019-08); no MOC coverage.
alternatives: one image only, so an image defect cannot be fully excluded; dust devils are frequent in northern Amazonis, and wind or a dust devil could darken a patch this size, though the spot is compact with no tracks in the 2 km crop; a small slope streak shed from the knob (the dark patch lies SE of it, but is round rather than a tapering fan)

name: western Acheron Fossae
size_m: ~65 (76x66), a darker core with a lighter patch on its W side
evidence: Compact dark spot about 65 m across (76 x 66 m at half depth on the 2 m grid) with a darker core and a lighter patch on its W side, on smooth ground on a trough floor in western Acheron Fossae, 380 km WSW of lead 90, in V22 2025-06-03 only (z -9.2 on a 30 m disc). Absent in seven earlier images from 2008 to 2025 (z +0.2 to +1.2), among them V19 2025-03-12 and V20 2025-04-13 under the same sun (incidence 43.1, 43.0 and 42.7 deg; r 0.46 and 0.42) and P20 2008-06-18 (r 0.66); J07 2016-09-02 was taken under a low sun (incidence 69 deg; r 0.35). The spot formed within 51 days, between 2025-04-13 and 2025-06-03. The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (84 x 72 m at half depth, z -1.7) and nowhere else in the 2 km crop. Control not informative (no comparably dark feature nearby). V19, V20 and V22 were each taken with a HiRISE image of a candidate impact site 18 to 20 km away that formed between 2018-04 and 2025-01, a separate and earlier event; V19 was aimed at that site. No HiRISE covers the spot (the nearest edge, of a 2023 image, is 1.7 km away); the nearest catalogued new impact is that site; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: one image only, so an image defect cannot be fully excluded, though the spot is round with a graded edge and V22 shows no line defect near it; a dust devil that stalled (no tracks in the 2 km crop); dark material shed from a slope (the nearest slope is about 120 m away and the spot is round, not a streak)

name: eastern Daedalia Planum, 555 km S of lead 18
size_m: ~75 (86x76), a dark core with small dark specks around it
evidence: Compact dark spot about 75 m across (86 x 76 m at half depth on the 2 m grid) with a dark core and several small dark specks within 150 m of it, on lava plains in eastern Daedalia Planum, 555 km S of lead 18, in V15 2024-11-19 only (z -6.1 on a 30 m disc). Absent in three earlier images, all aligned (z +0.1 to +0.3): P10 2007-08-15 (r 0.70; incidence 35.1 vs 43.2 deg), which is hazy because it was taken during the 2007 global dust storm, and B20 2010-04-04 and J22 2017-12-31 under a lower sun (incidence 62.8 and 63.9 deg; r 0.78 and 0.85). The bright patches around the site line up in all four images. U17 2023-02-11 is saturated at the site and is not used. The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (92 x 84 m at half depth, z -4.5) and nowhere else in the 2 km crop. Control not informative (no comparably dark feature nearby). Window 2017-12 to 2024-11; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 35.4 km); the nearest catalogued new impacts are two sites about 52 km away (two fresh craters on a lava flow imaged by HiRISE in 2012, and a CTX candidate site that formed between 2017-02 and 2021-01), separate events; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: one image only, so an image defect cannot be fully excluded, though the spot spans many image lines and has small specks around it; a dust devil that stalled (no tracks in the 2 km crop); the earlier images were taken under other suns (35 deg and hazy, or 63-64 deg, against 43), but none shows anything as dark

name: plains N of Tithonium Chasma, 58 km NE of lead 47
evidence: Compact dark spot about 25 m across (26 x 24 m at half depth on the 2 m grid) with a dark core on cratered plains N of Tithonium Chasma, 58 km NE of lead 47 and 123 km N of lead 88, in V21 2025-05-25 only (z -8.7 on a 20 m disc). Absent in four earlier images, all aligned (z -0.5 to -1.5): G22 2012-04-06 and 2012-04-23 (r 0.62 and 0.75), U18 2023-03-27 (r 0.73) and U22 2023-07-10 under the same sun (incidence 57.0 and 55.7 deg; r 0.54). The registered before/after difference is deepest at the spot (48 x 52 m at half depth, z -1.8) at the finer smoothing; at the coarser one a broad change at a corner of the 2 km crop is slightly deeper. A control feature (a small crater 276 m S) reads z -6.8 to -10.1 in every earlier image (positive). Window 2023-07 to 2025-05; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 15.3 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 18 km away (a cluster that formed between 2008-12 and 2010-09; Daubar 2022), a separate and older event; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: one image only, so an image defect cannot be fully excluded, though the spot spans several compression blocks of the image; a dust devil that stalled (no tracks in the 2 km crop)

name: floor of Tikhonravov crater, Arabia Terra
size_m: ~40 (38x36), a dark core in a diffuse halo ~150 m
evidence: Compact dark spot about 40 m across (38 x 36 m at half depth on the 2 m grid) with a dark core in a diffuse halo about 150 m across, mostly on its SW side, on the floor of Tikhonravov crater in Arabia Terra, 316 km WSW of lead 32, in V20 2025-04-04 only (z -4.6 on a 35 m disc). Absent in three earlier images, all aligned (z -0.2 to +0.1): B17 2010-01-14 under a similar sun (incidence 40.7 and 46.6 deg, azimuth 196 and 207 deg; r 0.60), and N06 2020-05-31 and N08 2020-07-25 under a lower sun (incidence 61.7 and 61.8 deg; r 0.57 and 0.36). A small crater about 120 m NNE of the spot shows in all four images. The registered before/after difference reaches z -2.7 at the spot (64 x 56 m at half depth); a broad change at the E edge of the 2 km crop is slightly deeper (z -3.1). A control feature 300 m NNW reads only z -0.6 to -1.9 in the earlier images (weak). Window 2020-07 to 2025-04; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 22.1 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 74 km away (a cluster that formed between 2008-03 and 2014-04; Daubar 2022), a separate and older event; no MOC coverage.
alternatives: one image only, so an image defect cannot be fully excluded, though the core and halo span many compression blocks of the heavily compressed V20; a dust devil that stalled (no tracks in the 2 km crop); the 2020 images were taken under a lower sun (62 deg), though a spot this dark would show under it

name: plains 272 km S of Medusae Fossae
size_m: ~190 (196x270), an irregular patch darkest in its NW part, no compact core
evidence: An irregular dark patch about 190 m across (196 x 270 m at half depth), darkest in its NW part, with lobes to the E and S, on rolling plains 272 km S of Medusae Fossae and 241 km from lead 67, in V21 2025-05-10 only (z -9.0 on a 60 m disc). Absent in F01 2014-04-06 under the same sun (incidence 58.9 vs 58.3 deg, azimuth 220 vs 221 deg; r 0.57 to 0.65; z -1.0); only these two CTX images cover the site. The registered before/after difference is deepest at the patch (z -2.5, 236 x 280 m at half depth), the deepest change in the 2 km crop, and a 5 x 5 km registered window shows no other new dark mark. A control feature 300 m S reads only z -1.6 in F01, so the control is weak. Window 2014-04 to 2025-05; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 20.5 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 24 km away (a candidate site that formed between 2014-07 and 2017-05, targeted by HiRISE and CTX in 2025), a separate event; no MOC coverage; 59.5 deg from InSight.
alternatives: wind stripping a thin bright dust layer from a patch (the patch is irregular, has no core and lies in dusty terrain), the main reason for the WEAK rating; a dust devil that stalled (no tracks in the 5 km window); one image only, though the patch spans about 35 x 50 CTX pixels, far larger than an image defect

name: terrain east of Gordii Dorsum (S of Olympus Mons)
evidence: Real darkening at nearly the same sun as 2024, but on a pre-existing faint dark mark (visible 2011, 2020, 2022) in ridged terrain full of ridge shadows; elongated along the ridges; one image.
alternatives: wind darkening of a small hollow; shading enhanced by clearer air (2024 image hazy, 17 deg off-nadir)

name: terrain west of Flammarion Crater
evidence: Compact dark dot on dusty Arabia Terra plains, absent 2010 and 2020 under the same sun; no landform at the spot before.
alternatives: noise cluster or compression artifact in a heavily compressed single image

name: Mangala Valles
evidence: Elongated dark streak about 90 x 30 m (a 94 x 54 m box at half depth on the 2 m grid), a teardrop with its broad end to the WNW, on smooth ground NW of a rough slope in Mangala Valles, 401 km WSW of lead 20, in V21 2025-05-13 only (z -4.6 on a 25 m disc). Absent in six earlier CTX images from 2006 to 2023 (z +0.1 to +0.4), among them U19 2023-04-28 and V01 2023-09-18 under nearly the same sun (incidence 55.6, 62.6 and 59.9 deg, azimuth 219, 218 and 223 deg). The figure's alignment scores are low (r -0.47 to 0.29), so each placement was checked by matching band-passed ground in four parts of the scene (scripts/ground_offset.py). F10 and V01 share V21's detector striping and image edges, which the registration matched instead of the ground, so they are placed by these ground offsets (matching scores 0.41 to 0.85); the other four images match the ground at 0.50 to 0.89. MOC E16/00999 (2002-05-15), registered to V21 with 17 feature matches, shows nothing at the spot (z +1.1) but a similar WNW-ESE dark streak about 130 m NE, absent in every CTX image from 2006 on, while a fainter streak about 290 m WNW shows in both 2002 and 2025 (lead97_mangala_valles_moc_2002.png). The registered before/after difference is dominated by V21's image edge at a corner of the 2 km crop (not informative). That fainter streak, used as the control, reads z -3.8 in U19 under nearly the same sun and -2.9 in V21, but -1.5 to +2.4 in the other earlier images. Window 2023-09 to 2025-05; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 9.7 km; the HiRISE image taken with V01 is of layers around a streamlined form); the nearest catalogued new impact is 73 km away (a CTX candidate site that formed between 2010-10 and 2018-01).
alternatives: a wind streak or a dust-devil track segment: a dark streak of the same orientation and size appeared 130 m away by 2002 and was gone by 2006, so streaks like this form and fade at the site; one image only; a teardrop rather than a round spot, though an oblique impact can make an elongated dark zone

name: Sulci Gordii, E of Olympus Mons
size_m: ~35 (28x40), a dark core with a short faint tail to the S
evidence: Compact dark spot about 35 m across (28 x 40 m at half depth on the 2 m grid) with a short faint tail to the S, on lightly ridged plains in Sulci Gordii, 317 km E of the Olympus Mons summit and 318 km NW of lead 6, in V20 2025-04-04 only (z -7.4 on a 25 m disc), which is heavily compressed. Absent in two earlier images, both from 2020 (z +2.1 and +1.8): N08 2020-07-25 and N11 2020-10-25, taken under a lower sun from another direction (incidence 64.0 and 52.8 vs 45.3 deg, azimuth 150 and 144 vs 203 deg), both strongly striped and poorly aligned (r 0.22 and 0.37). The registered before/after difference reaches z -2.4 at the spot (44 x 60 m at half depth); a broad change near a corner of the 2 km crop is deeper (z -3.7). The control is weak (a feature 290 m N reads only z -1.4 and -1.5 in the earlier images and -0.3 in V20). MOC S06/00674 (2005-05-08) covers the site but has no map-projected product, and its non-projected gallery image could not be registered (2 consistent feature matches of 7). Window 2020-10 to 2025-04; no image aimed at an impact; no HiRISE (nearest edge 9.5 km); the nearest catalogued new impact is 52 km away (a cluster that formed between 2012-11 and 2016-11; Daubar 2022), a separate event.
alternatives: a noise cluster or compression artifact in a single heavily compressed image (the spot is only about 5 x 7 CTX pixels); a shading or albedo difference seen only under V20's sun, since no earlier image has comparable light; a dust devil that stalled

evidence: shading under the sun from the south-west: a dark mark on fractured ground, 0.3055N 164.1289E, dark in G23 2012-05-10 and N22 2021-09-07 (sun azimuth 217 deg; z -3.5, -2.9) and not in G07 2011-01-16, U17 2023-02-18 or V16 2024-12-06 (azimuth 168 to 201 deg; z -0.6 to -1.3); already there in G23, nine years before the discovery image

landform shading: a dark patch on the shaded side of a landform, 19.9700N 51.0326E, darkest in K23 2019-11-28 and N22 2021-09-24 (z -3.9 and -4.7), both with the sun from azimuth 201 to 203 deg, weaker in the five images of 2020 to 2022 with the sun from azimuth 139 to 155 deg (z +0.2 to -2.3); the only earlier image, K13 2019-01-24 (azimuth 140 deg; z -0.2), is hazy; the darkness follows the sun; no new spot

pit shading: the dark mark is the shaded inside of a small hollow in pitted plains, -8.0173N 176.2136E, whose dark curved rim shows in every image (B09 2009-05-27, J04 2016-06-12, J05 2016-07-10; z -0.7, -0.3, 0.0); darkest in U09 2022-06-08 (z -2.4), under a sun 8 deg lower than B09's from nearly the same direction (incidence 52.3 vs 44.5 deg, azimuth 164 vs 158 deg), and fainter again in V01 2023-09-17 and V07 2024-03-17 (z -1.6, -1.3); U19 2023-04-11 does not align (r 0.0); shading, not a new spot

growing diffuse dark patch: a diffuse dark zone several hundred metres across with no compact core on plains south of Schiaparelli crater, -5.4833N 14.4838E, faint in B09 2009-05-06 (r 0.39; z -0.3), darker in N10 2020-09-17 (z -2.0), U11 2022-08-09 (z -2.8) and W08 2026-03-14 (z -3.6), with dark streaks around it in W08; it keeps darkening over six years instead of fading, as wind-driven removal of dust beside dark dunes does; not a new spot

pre-existing dark patch in mottled terrain: the patch, -1.1964N 2.3967E, is one of many dark patches of a mottled surface and shows in D09 2013-02-21, D10 2013-03-16, K04 2018-04-17, U17 2023-02-13 and U18 2023-03-13 (z -2.0 to -2.7); the discovery image, U12 2022-09-14, is washed out (z -3.7), and none of the 2007-2008 images aligns usefully (P10 r 0.16, P18 r 0.02, P20 r 0.38 but washed out at the site), so no clear image shows the ground without it

knob shadow possible: a dark patch on knobby ground, 1.8940N 159.5946E, in one image, U12 2022-09-18 (z -5.2), with the sun from azimuth 153 deg; the three earlier images, P17 2008-03-13, P22 2008-08-16 and K18 2019-06-16 (z -1.2, -0.9 and -0.5), had the sun from azimuth 207 to 215 deg, 54 to 62 deg away in direction (incidence 41 to 56 vs 42 deg), so the patch may be a knob's shadow that only U12's sun casts; one image under a different sun direction; 24.1 deg from InSight, inside the Bickel area

ridge shading under a new sun direction: a dark mark on the crest of a ridge, 13.6737N 268.5505E, dark only under the sun from azimuth 147 to 151 deg (K08 2018-08-23, K09 2018-09-09, U13 2022-10-10; z -1.1, -1.4, -2.7) and not under the sun from 180 to 188 deg (P03 2007-01-01, P03 2007-01-28, K04 2018-04-15; z +3.1, +0.9, +2.0); shading, not a new spot

washed-out image: U14 2022-11-25 is hazy and washed out at the site, 22.8708N 281.2457E, and its faint smudge (z -5.6) cannot be checked, since the earlier P21 2008-07-05, G17 2011-11-23 and N10 2020-09-27 do not align with it (r -0.01 to 0.16; z -0.4 to +0.2)

pre-existing trough floor: the dark mark is the shaded floor of a bend in a narrow fracture trough, 22.0996N 146.8382E, already dark in P13 2007-11-26 (z -1.9) and in U15 2022-12-07 (z -2.2) under similar suns (incidence 40.4 and 43.3 deg), fainter in P02 2006-12-19 (z -0.3) under a lower sun from the south (incidence 51.7 deg, azimuth 182 against 154 to 156 deg); P10 2007-08-02 does not cover it; shading of a pre-existing trough, not a new spot

noisy, striped image: nothing is visible by eye at the spot, 3.4292N 159.5884E, in U15 2022-12-09 (z -3.5), which has the sun 30 deg away in direction from the only earlier image, P17 2008-03-13 (azimuth 178 vs 208 deg, incidence 36.8 vs 45.2 deg; r 0.70; z -0.2); the same image's detection r00, 11 km SSE, is a separate, visible spot

active dust devil's shadow or image defect: a very dark, sharp-edged lens ~250 m long and ~30 m wide running roughly N-S at the edge of a bright plateau, 15.2979N 23.4084E, in one image only, U15 2022-12-26 (z -2.2), absent in P13 2007-11-23, B03 2008-11-07 and K11 2018-11-30 (z +0.8, +0.4, +1.1); it runs away from the sun (azimuth 168 deg) as the shadow of an active dust devil would; not a new impact spot

slope streak on a pre-existing scarp: a thin E-W dark line ~150 m long with a bright patch at its east end, -10.2347N 204.6372E, there in B17 2010-01-08 and N15 2021-02-07 (z +0.3, +1.3), became a darker wedge about 130 x 25 m widening westward in U16 2023-01-02 (z -2.7) under nearly N15's sun (incidence 40.2 vs 42.7 deg, azimuth 202 vs 197 deg); a real change, but a wedge widening along a slope from a point is the shape of a slope streak, not of an impact

transient dark mark: a sharp dark V ~150 m across, 18.0743N 266.1281E, in U16 2023-01-04 only (z -3.7); gone in V07 2024-03-30 (incidence 65 deg; z -0.6) and absent in five images from 2008-03 to 2022-06 (z +0.1 to -0.4; -1.7 in B19 2010-03-23, when transient dark patches were nearby); most likely a short-lived dust-removal mark, though a fast-fading blast zone of an oblique impact cannot be excluded; nearest known impact 38.5 km (ESP_067548_1985)

diffuse wind-streak patch: a dark patch on the W side of a ~70 m crater, 8.7731N 270.3390E, in one image, U16 2023-01-15 (z -5.3); in the only earlier image, G18 2011-12-13 (z -0.4), E-W dark streaks extend toward the crater, and they are gone by 2023; a wind-driven albedo change at a crater, no compact new spot

image problem (a streak defect): the dark mark, 8.9165N 270.2574E, lies in a block of horizontal streak lines in U16 2023-01-15 (z -5.0); the only earlier images, B09 2009-05-19 and G18 2011-12-13 (z +0.2 and +0.7), show plain ground; one image and a defect at the spot, no ground feature

washed-out image: U17 2023-02-12 is washed out and almost featureless at the site, 38.9369N 270.9310E; its z -3.9 comes from faint broad shading and no mark is visible by eye; P12 2007-10-27, G15 2011-09-17 and K08 2018-08-19 (z -0.1 to 0.0) show nothing there either

scarp-edge shading: a dark mark at the lip of a scarp between smooth upper plains and etched ground, 13.8977N 22.1327E, dark in every image under a sun from azimuth 192 to 207 deg (P19 2008-05-02, D20 2014-01-18, D21 2014-02-20, U17 2023-02-28; z -1.8 to -2.3) and absent only in P12 2007-10-15 under a sun from 150 deg (z +0.2); already there in 2008, so shading of a pre-existing scarp, not a new spot

new slope streak from a ridge: an elongated dark streak ~300 m long tapering to the ESE from a knob on a sinuous ridge, -13.0860N 214.0676E, in one image, U19 2023-04-02 (z -2.2), absent in G21 2012-03-26, F04 2014-07-29 and J04 2016-06-25 (z -0.2, -0.1, -0.1; F09 2014-12-05 does not cover it); a new slope or wind streak, a real change but common, not a compact spot

new diffuse streak: a soft-edged dark streak ~280 x 80 m running NW from the rim of a small crater, 13.7392S 214.1498E, in one image, U19 2023-04-02 (z -5.1); not in G21 2012-03-26 or F04 2014-07-29 (z 0.0 in both); F09 2014-12-05 and J04 2016-06-25 undecided; elongated without a compact core, a wind streak or dust-devil track, not an impact spot

pre-existing dark spot: the spot, 24.9911N 229.1602E, is already there in B17 2010-01-03 (z -2.8) and in F19 2015-10-09, K04 2018-04-29, K17 2019-05-12 and U19 2023-04-06 (z -2.5, -1.6, -2.0 and -4.2); only P11 2007-09-26, hazy from the 2007 global dust storm (r 0.25; z -0.3), lacks it, so no clear image shows the ground without it

knob shadow: a dark patch on the shaded side of a knob, 3.2510N 144.0522E, darkest in U19 2023-04-21 (z -13.4) with the sun from azimuth 213 deg, also dark in D02 2012-07-27 and K18 2019-06-07 (z -5.8 and -3.3; azimuth 203 and 209 deg), but not in P07 2007-05-16, N07 2020-06-05 or U09 2022-06-02 (z +0.4, -0.1 and +0.1; azimuth 158 to 170 deg); the dark patch follows the sun, so not an impact spot

ridge shading: an elongated dark mark along the ridges of ridged terrain, 10.3601N 209.6225E, in U20 2023-05-05 (z -5.6; sun azimuth 207 deg), already there in N06 2020-05-05 under a lower sun (z -2.0); B18 2010-02-01 and G05 2010-11-10 read +0.6 and +1.0; elongated along the ridges, shading or a wind feature, not a compact spot

slope streak: a fan-shaped dark streak widening downslope from a point, on a slope among the pedestal craters SW of Olympus Mons, 10.4900N 218.3510E, only in U20 2023-05-07 (z -2.8); not in P19 2008-05-03 or P21 2008-07-04 (r 0.74, 0.63; z -0.3, -0.6); N08 2020-07-17 and U17 2023-02-01 do not align well (r 0.26); a slope streak, not an impact

slope streak: a fan-shaped dark streak on a slope among the pedestal craters SW of Olympus Mons, 10.4891N 218.3440E, in U20 2023-05-07 (z -2.8) and faintly in U17 2023-02-01 (r 0.46; z -0.6), not in P19 2008-05-03 or P21 2008-07-04 (z -0.1, -0.3); its shape, widening downslope from a point, is that of a slope streak; the same image's detection r00, 0.4 km E, is another

pre-existing dark hollow: a dark-toned hollow among knobs, 3.3378N 124.0434E, dark in all six images from F05 2014-08-19 to U20 2023-05-15 (z -1.3 to -5.1, varying with the sun) and faintly in the washed-out P07 2007-05-12 (r 0.29; z -0.6); not a new spot

wind-streak albedo feature, already there in 2010: an elongated NW-SE dark streak ~400 m long on wind-etched plains, -9.3550N 225.2290E, already marked by dark patches in G03 2010-09-18 (z -0.6) and longer in G23 2012-05-28 and U20 2023-05-24 (z -1.4, -2.5); elongated and older than 2012, not a new compact spot (55 km from L156, found in the same image pair)

noisy, striped and blocky image: a N-S dark mark ~25 x 60 m, 17.4291N 265.0670E, in one image, U20 2023-05-27 (z -3.2), which is striped and blocky from compression at the site; the mark runs along the stripes and is about one compression block wide, so it cannot be told from noise; the only earlier image, F03 2014-06-26 (r 0.51; z -0.4), shows nothing there, and there is no later image

diffuse darkening: a broad dark zone ~300 m across with no compact core below an E-W scarp, -10.9437N 234.6154E, darkest in U20 2023-05-31 (incidence 60.7 deg; z -3.1 on a 120 m disc) and fainter but present in B01 2008-09-22 under nearly the same sun (incidence 60.4 deg; r 0.77; z -0.1) and in G03 and G04 2010 (z -0.7 to -1.4); a wind-driven change in dust cover, not a new spot

pre-existing knob: the dark NW tip of a field of rugged knobs, -6.0631N 265.6760E, the same in P02 2006-12-31 (z -1.4) as in F18 2015-09-24, F23 2016-02-14 and U21 2023-06-01 (z -3.2 to -4.9); B01 2008 is unaligned (r 0.03); no new spot

faint ragged mark: an irregular dark patch ~70 x 20 m elongated E-W among small knobs and ridges, 20.7318N 208.9068E, in U21 2023-06-01 and V20 2025-04-05 (z -2.3 and -1.6 on a 62 m disc); absent in B19 2010-03-17 under the same sun (incidence 42.9 vs 46.1 and 44.2 deg, azimuth 200 deg; r 0.82; z -0.3); no compact core, and the knobby ground has many similar dark marks, so a small slope streak or a piece of a dust-devil track is as likely as an impact

pre-existing crater: a small crater ~40 m across beside an old dark band on plains, 0.9086S 132.3610E, in all seven images from B18 2010-02-24 to U21 2023-06-08; its shaded interior reads darker in N10_066392 2020-09-24 and U21 (z -1.7 and -3.1 on an 87 m disc) than in B18, F03, J05 and K04 (z -0.6 to -1.3), with the sun at azimuth 156 and 218 deg against 181 to 214 deg and lower in U21; no new dark spot

slope shading: a diffuse dark patch on a slope, 11.1438S 171.6810E, in U19 2023-04-10, U21 2023-06-10 and V22 2025-06-08 (z -4.0, -4.0 and -3.9), all with the sun from azimuth 220 to 224 deg; G03 2010-09-02 (azimuth 212 deg) reads -1.1 and J06 2016-08-22 and N06 2020-05-25 (azimuth 180 deg) -0.5 and -0.7; the darkness follows the sun's direction; no compact spot

diffuse darkening: a broad, soft-edged dark patch ~400 m across beside a small crater, 3.1099S 9.9737E, first in K18 2019-06-24 (z -4.6 on a 140 m disc) and still there in U19 2023-04-17 and U21 2023-06-16 (z -2.7); absent in P07 2007, P19 2008 and G18 2011 (r 0.48 to 0.51); no compact core, so a change of dust cover, not an impact spot

diffuse darkening: a faint soft-edged dark patch ~150 m without a core on plains, 2.2990N 205.6849E, with a second faint patch ~600 m N, in one image, U21 2023-06-17 (z -2.8 on a 134 m disc); not in P20 2008-06-14, the only earlier image, under the same sun (incidence 52.3 vs 54.3 deg, azimuth 216 deg; r 0.94; z +1.1); too faint and diffuse for a lead

probable slope streaks: an irregular dark patch ~150 x 100 m with a darker core and lobes on hummocky ground, 37.3338N 269.2733E, new between N16 2021-03-07 and U20 2023-05-23 (also in U21 2023-06-20 and 2023-06-25; z -2.4 to -3.8); absent in P17 2008, G17 2011 and N16 2021 (r 0.62 to 0.69); a registered 5 km window shows at least two larger new dark patches formed in the same interval, an elongated streak several hundred metres long ~1.4 km SE and a broad patch ~2 km W, so it is one of a group of new dark streaks on this dusty terrain, not a lone impact

transient dark mark: a C-shaped dark mark ~60 m across, 35.5100N 222.3819E, only in U22 2023-07-02 (incidence 43.7 deg, azimuth 188 deg; z -3.4); not seen in V16 2024-12-25 or in V20 2025-04-08, the latter under nearly the same sun (incidence 42.4 deg, azimuth 184 deg; r 0.76; z -1.3), nor in four earlier images from 2008-07 to 2023-02 (z -0.6 to +0.1); not a lasting spot

active dust devil: in one image, U22 2023-07-09 (incidence 44 deg, sun from the W at a bearing of 272 deg, 15:21 local time), a pitch-black lobed patch ~100 x 40 m elongated E-W at 34.3393N 203.8940E (z -2.5 on a 100 m disc) lies 800 m due E of a bright blob ~50 m across, i.e. exactly where the shadow of a dust column ~800 m tall would fall; a small dark spot lies between them; none of the three is in N22 2021-09-05 (r 0.52), P03 2007-01-05 or P01 2006-11-13 (r 0.83 and 0.70); the 2006-2007 images were taken to monitor dust raising in northern Amazonis Planitia; 55 km NW of L91

pre-existing dark mark: a dark arc ~50 m at 21.3046N 15.1880E, already in F01 2014-04-26 (z -1.5 once re-centred on matched ground; the pipeline's registration had r 0.34), is a darker, compact ~30 m blob in U18 2023-03-27 and U22 2023-07-10 (z -4.5 and -7.4); all three images are heavily compressed; 12.5 km from L118, in the same images; a new impact on the old mark cannot be excluded but is not shown

probable fresh slope streak: a pitch-black lens-shaped mark ~170 x 50 m, elongated E-W on a massif slope that carries older slope streaks, 16.5517N 234.2282E, in one image (U22 2023-07-20; z -3.3); absent in P02 2006-12-19 and J03 2016-05-23 (r 0.45 and 0.75); U13 2022-10 and U16 2023-01 are unaligned (r 0.04 and 0.00); no later image; the E-W shape does not fit a dust-devil shadow under a SSW sun; on a steep slope a fresh streak is the likeliest cause, though an impact cannot be excluded on one image

diffuse darkening: a soft-edged dark patch ~200 m without a core where shallow troughs cross in textured terrain, 2.6538S 143.6034E, in N22 2021-09-09, U22 2023-07-24 and V21 2025-05-11 (z -3.0, -3.1 and -2.4 on a 140 m disc); not in B20 2010-04-22 under a similar sun (incidence 56.0 vs 57.5 to 62.6 deg, azimuth 222 vs 219 to 221 deg; r 0.64; z +0.2) or G04 2010-10-16 (r 0.56; z +0.5); the troughs are dark in every image; no compact spot

shading at a yardang end: a dark mark at the end of a small yardang among wind-carved ridges, 4.8032N 229.2957E, dark in U22 2023-07-30 and V22 2025-06-09 (z -2.2, -1.4) under a sun from azimuth 214 to 215 deg but absent in V05 2024-01-16 (z +0.1), after the discovery image, under a sun from 183 deg, and in U18 2023-03-03 (z -0.3); it comes and goes with the sun direction, so shading, not a new spot

pre-existing small crater: the dark spot, 4.5615N 14.1530E (~40 m; z -5.1 in U22 2023-07-31, also dark in U15 2022-12-24), sits on a small crater whose shaded wall shows in B18 2010-02-17 and in G19 and D01 2012; faint again in V14 2024-10-10 under the same sun as U15 (incidence 37 deg), so most likely dark material moving in and out of the crater rather than a new impact

image problem: the earlier image G22 2012-04-12 is heavily striped, and the darkening at -12.1384N 246.2586E in U23 2023-08-02 and V21 2025-05-04 (z -2.7 on a 59 m disc) is not a distinct spot, only the shadows of small knobs

slope streak: two parallel dark streaks ~500 m long on the slope of a hill, 11.7395N 24.3116E: the first new in J04 2016-06-16, the second beside it by U23 2023-08-02 (z -2.7 on a 120 m disc); absent in G03 2010 and in G22 and D02 2012 (r 0.80 to 0.81); new slope streaks, not an impact spot

crater shading under a new sun direction: the dark mark is the shaded inside of a crater, -9.0608N 150.1274E, that is in every image; dark when the sun comes from azimuth 202 to 221 deg (U23 2023-08-10, V04 2023-12-10, V17 2025-01-11; z -3.0, -2.3, -3.1) and not under the sun from 158 to 189 deg (P04 2007-02-17, P08 2007-06-02, N08 2020-07-14, N10 2020-09-17, U10 2022-07-28; z -1.4 to +0.5); shading, not a new spot

long-lived diffuse patch: a soft-edged dark patch ~300 m across without a compact core, 5.8773S 10.9331E, in all 17 images from B12 2009-08-13 to V20 2025-04-20 (z -1.8 to -6.3) and fainter in P02 2006-12-08, P18 2008-04-13 and B03 2008-11-04 (z -0.9, -2.1 and -2.0); its contrast varies with the sun and the image quality; no compact spot

slope streak: the lower end of one of several dark streaks running SW down a slope below a knobby scarp, 30.5351N 273.5427E; absent in P15 2008-01-13 and D22 2014-03-15 (r 0.29 and 0.62; z +0.1 and -0.7), new by N10 2020-09-09 and clearest in U23 2023-08-19 (z -4.7); a new streak on a slope, not an impact spot

knob-flank shading: a dark area on the flank of a low mound, 29.3053N 139.8278E, already dark in P15 2008-01-08, P16 2008-02-05 and N15 2021-02-26 (z +0.2, -0.5, -0.1, the mound's dark flank falling in the surroundings); darker in U23 2023-08-26 (z -2.5) under a sun from azimuth 193 deg against 161 to 170 deg before; shading of the flank under a new sun direction, not a new spot

diffuse darkening: a broad soft-edged dark patch ~300 m across without a core, crossed by dark streaks, NE of a ~350 m crater, 30.3842N 287.1655E, in U23 2023-08-27, V02 2023-10-27 and V03 2023-11-01 (z -3.1, -4.1 and -1.9 on a 120 m disc); a fainter dark patch is already there in K13 2019-01-05, K16 2019-04-26 and N15 2021-02-07 (z -0.8, -1.3 and -1.1; r 0.29 to 0.61); P22 2008-08-14 and N15 2021-02-18 read -0.8 and -0.4 (r 0.81 and 0.67); dark linear tracks cross the area from 2021 on; no compact spot

slope streaks: dark streaks running down the flanks of ridges, 0.5186N 195.3725E, first in K15 2019-03-05 and in every image after it to V14 2024-10-24 (z -1.0 to -2.7), not in five images from 2006-12-06 to 2018-02-09 (z -0.3 to -0.8); elongated downslope streaks, not a compact spot

diffuse darkening: the floor of a shallow hollow ~250 m across in hummocky terrain, 2.0649S 222.2564E, reads dark in U21 2023-06-03 and V01 2023-09-26 (z -3.3 and -5.7 on a 140 m disc) but not in P21 2008-07-26 (z -0.9; r 0.58) under a similar sun (incidence 57 vs 56 and 60 deg, azimuth 219 vs 218 and 214 deg), where the hollow's shaded rim already shows; no compact core in U21; a change of the hollow's dust cover, not an impact spot

9.5007N 193.8749E: a diffuse mottled dark patch ~90 m among knob shadows on knobby ground, in one image (V02 2023-10-08; z -4.9 on a 122 m disc); absent in G02 2010-08-10 (r 0.41) under a similar sun; the only later image (V12 2024-08-02, r 0.17, sun from another azimuth) shows at most a faint smudge; too diffuse to separate from shading on one image

slope streaks: dark streaks running down a scarp in Tempe Fossae, 39.6097N 284.6720E, in V02 2023-10-16 (z -3.0) and W01 2025-08-16 (r 0.02; z -3.4), not in B17 2010-01-26 (r 0.67; z -0.6); K09 2018-09-13 and 2018-09-18 (incidence 74 deg) are too oblique to tell; elongated downslope streaks, not a compact spot; the 2012-2018 impact site that K09 2018-09-18 was aimed at is 84 km away

slope streaks: a set of new dark streaks ~300 m long running downslope on a textured slope, 32.0657N 149.0220E, in V02 2023-10-16 (z -2.4 on a 140 m disc); absent in the nine earlier images from P01 2006-11-23 to G23 2012-05-02

Amazonis Planitia, 35.2720N 190.3592E: a compact dark spot ~40 m, absent in F04 2014-07-15 and J17 2017-07-09 (r 0.68 and 0.77; z -0.1 and 0.0) and present in all seven images from U06 2022-03-05 to V07 2024-03-10 (z -8.6 in U06, -4.8 in V02 2023-10-24); no image between 2017-07 and 2022-03, so the window contains the S1094b impact of 2021-12-24 (Posiolova et al. 2022), 28.0 km ENE of its catalogued position (35.1011N 189.8200E); HiRISE ESP_082308_2155 (2024-02-16), aimed at 'Secondary craters associated with large fresh impact in Amazonis Planitia', is centred 6.7 km away and ends 2.2 km from the spot, so that impact's secondaries reach this area; probably a secondary of that recorded impact, set aside as part of a known event

Amazonis Planitia, 34.9593N 189.9074E: the mark logged as V19_087226_2154_r03 (same site as V19_087226_2154_r03), a dark mark in a shallow circular feature in the field of secondary craters of the S1094b impact (formed 2021-12-24, detected by InSight; Posiolova et al. 2022), found again in V16_086303_2136; 0.28 km (78 m W, 274 m S) from that mark's position, within the map offsets between the CTX images; set aside with it as part of that recorded impact

Amazonis Planitia, 34.9431N 189.9142E: a dark mark 10.4 km SSE of the catalogued position of the S1094b crater (35.1011N 189.8200E; formed 2021-12-24, detected by InSight; Posiolova et al. 2022; CTX 'Candidate impact site formed between Dec 24 2021 and Dec 25 2021') and 1.25 km S of the mark logged as V19_087226_2154_r03, inside that impact's field of secondary craters with dark markings; absent in G18 2011-12-14 (r 0.88, z +0.7); the mid-2022 images were taken under a very low sun (incidence 73-75 deg), where the mark is muted (V08 2024-04-18, at 74 deg, reads only z -1.25 while it was surely there), and U09_074633 2022-06-28 already reads -2.6; clear in thirteen images 2022-11-13 to 2025-02-17 under a higher sun (z -1.7 to -4.9 on a 66 m disc); HiRISE ESP_073710_2155 (2022-04-17) and ESP_086303_2155 cover it; probably a secondary or ejecta of that recorded impact, set aside as part of a known event

Tempe Terra, 37.8123N 280.4306E: a small dark dot ~20 m among knobs, absent in B19 and B22 2010 under the same sun as the later images (incidence 41-43 deg) and in K09 2018-09-12 (low sun, 73 deg), present in 13 images from 2022-03-17 to 2025-08-31 under high and low suns; it lies 22.8 km SE of the S1000a impact (2021-09-18, a crater cluster up to 130 m detected by InSight; Posiolova et al. 2022; CTX 'Candidate impact site formed Sept 18th 2021', HiRISE 'Fresh impact crater in Tempe Terra', 11 images 2022-2025, whose CTX ride-alongs are most of these images) and formed in a window that contains that date; very probably a secondary crater or ejecta of that recorded impact, set aside as part of a known event

InSight lander's retrorocket blast zone (landed 2018-11-26; a dark spot ~20 m in radius in HiRISE, Golombek et al. 2020): spot at 4.5007N 135.6195E in the CTX frame, 254 m WSW of the lander's HiRISE position 4.5024N 135.6234E, within the CTX map-frame error seen at other sites (200 to 600 m; the heat shield and backshell lie 762 m NE and 553 m SE); absent in five images 2014-07-09 to 2016-12-10, faint 2018-12-16 (z -1.7), clear 2019-05-04 (z -3.9) and from 2019-09-23 on (z -9.7 in 2019, -4.5 in 2023, -2.3 to -4.0 in 2025); found blind, a check on the pipeline
